### 🐛 Describe the bug A server started with `--api-key` refuses unauthenticated requests on `/v1/*`, as documented. The same requests are **served** when posted to `/invocations`, which dispatches to the same handlers and is not covered by the guard. Measured with `--api-key SECRET-KEY-123` and **no** `Authorization` header: | request | 0.27.1 | 0.29.0 | |---|---|---| | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | 401 | 401 | | `POST /v1/completions` | 401 | 401 | | **`POST /invocations`** (chat body) | **200, full completion** | **200, full completion** | | **`POST /invocations`** (completions body) | **200, full completion** | **200, full completion** | No special flags: a plain `vllm serve --api-key ` on one GPU. **Related to but distinct from CVE-2026-22778. That CVE was the video-processing RCE reachable via this route (fixed in 0.14.1).** _The api-key bypass property of /invocations itself was not the subject of that fix and still holds on 0.27.1 and 0.29.0; the SageMaker router is mounted unconditionally (no SageMaker flag, no dev-mode gate), so every --api-key operator gets an unauthenticated inference path they did not opt into._ **Cause** The guard is a path-prefix test (0.27.1 `entrypoints/serve/utils/server_utils.py:42`, 0.29.0 `entrypoints/serve/middleware/authenticate.py:11`): ```python GUARDED_PREFIX = ("/v1", "/v2", "/inference", "/cohere") ... if url_path.startswith(GUARDED_PREFIX) and not self.verify_token(headers): return JSONResponse(content={"error": "Unauthorized"}, status_code=401) ``` `/invocations` is mounted at the root, and **unconditionally** — there is no SageMaker flag and no dev-mode gate: ```python register_sagemaker_api_router(app, supported_tasks, model_config) # api_server.py ``` So on every vLLM deployment the SageMaker entrypoint is present, it forwards a request body to the ordinary chat/completions handlers, and the prefix test never sees it. ### Reproduction Use this: [repro_api_key_bypass.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/99df19c52a4383e5e328be02baaceddc#file-repro_api_key_bypass-py) `python3 repro_api_key_bypass.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model --api-key ` Start any model with `--api-key `. The script sends the *same* body to `/v1/chat/completions` and to `/invocations` with no credentials and prints both statuses; it exits non-zero when the guarded route refuses and the unguarded one serves. An operator who sets `--api-key` has exactly one authentication mechanism, and it does not hold. Anyone who can reach the port gets unrestricted inference: * compute is consumed without authorisation; * anything the deployment attaches server-side — a system prompt, a chat template's instructions, retrieved context, tools — is reachable by an unauthenticated caller; * rate limiting or accounting keyed on the API key does not see this traffic at all. The vLLM security guide's firewall advice is to "block all incoming connections except to the TCP port the API server is [on]", i.e. that port is the intended exposed surface, which is where this route lives. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Performance]: Qwen3.5 native MTP can be slower than no-MTP CUDA graph baseline despite good acceptance
body:
## Summary

We are benchmarking a Qwen3.5 OCR checkpoint with native MTP support in vLLM. The model has a lightweight native MTP branch:

- `mtp_num_hidden_layers=1`
- `mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings=false`

In our OCR workload, MTP acceptance is not terrible. MTP1 reaches around `82%-88%` acceptance, and MTP2 can reach mean accepted length above `2.3`. However, end-to-end throughput in graph mode is still below the best no-MTP vLLM baseline.

The main issue seems to be that the vLLM spec decode execution path adds enough per-step overhead to erase the theoretical benefit from fewer decode steps. This is particularly visible with `num_speculative_tokens=2`, where rejection sampling, metadata preparation, slot mapping, and `num_computed_tokens` updates become large overheads.

We would like to understand whether this is expected for native Qwen MTP today, whether `num_speculative_tokens > 1` currently requires repeated forward/processing through the same MTP layer, and whether there are planned optimizations for the graph-mode spec decode path.

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.23.0`
- PyTorch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- GPU: NVIDIA L20X
- Tensor parallel: `1`
- CUDA graph mode: enabled, `enforce_eager=false`
- Workload: multimodal OCR / document parsing, long outputs
- Decode temperature: `0`

Main generation config:

```text
max_new_tokens=16384
max_model_len=32768
max_num_batched_tokens=32768
gpu_memory_utilization=0.8
max_num_seqs=None
```

We intentionally did not give MTP a larger `max_num_seqs` or give baseline a smaller one. Both paths use the same input subset and batching-related configuration.

## Speculative configs tested

MTP1:

```json
{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1,"use_local_argmax_reduction":true}
```

MTP2:

```json
{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2,"use_local_argmax_reduction":true}
```

## Results

### n64 graph-mode clean benchmark

| mode | tok/s | req/s | bench sec | output tokens | finish | acceptance | mean accept length | per-position acceptance |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| no-MTP baseline | 2246.73 | 1.381 | 46.35 | 104138 | `stop:64` | - | - | - |
| MTP1 | 1926.41 | 1.181 | 54.21 | 104432 | `stop:64` | 82.83% | 1.828 | 82.83% |
| MTP2 | 1821.76 | 1.119 | 57.17 | 104152 | `stop:64` | 66.77% | 2.335 | 78.21%, 55.34% |

MTP1 is about `0.86x` of the no-MTP graph baseline, not a speedup.

MTP2 has a higher mean accepted length, but still does not beat the best no-MTP graph baseline. The second speculative token acceptance is also much lower than the first token.

### n32 timing benchmark after local instrumentation

| mode | tok/s | output tokens | finish | acceptance | mean accept length |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| no-MTP baseline | 1898.19 | 29017 | `stop:32` | - | - |
| MTP1 before local Triton patch | 1824.31 | 29024 | `stop:32` | 88.06% | 1.881 |
| MTP1 after local Triton patch | 1980.96 | 29016 | `stop:32` | 88.08% | 1.881 |
| MTP2 after local Triton patch | 2172.36 | 28972 | `stop:32` | 76.03% | 2.521 |

The n32 timing case is not our final speed claim; it is mostly for profiling. It suggests that some overhead can be reduced, but the larger n64 graph-mode benchmark still does not show a stable MTP speedup over the best no-MTP baseline.

## Timing hotspots

With local timing instrumentation, MTP2 n32 shows the following cumulative costs:

| item | cumulative time |
| --- | ---: |
| `gpu_draft_total` | 3017.8 ms |
| `runner_prepare_inputs` | 2276.5 ms |
| `reject_sample_kernel` | 1702.8 ms |
| `gpu_target_forward` | 1357.8 ms |
| `prepare_num_computed_gpu` | 1033.5 ms |
| `prepare_num_computed_update_kernel` | 1016.9 ms |
| `step35_loop_update_positions` | 668.5 ms |
| `prepare_compute_slot_mapping` | 603.1 ms |

Before our local patch, `prepare_num_computed_gpu` was one of the clearest overheads. In MTP1 n32, we observed:

| item | baseline | MTP1 before patch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `prepare_num_computed_gpu` | 6.4 ms | 626.7 ms |
| `runner_prepare_inputs` | 529.8 ms | 1346.0 ms |
| `gpu_target_forward` | 858.0 ms | 1243.5 ms |
| `gpu_draft_total` | - | 531.5 ms |

We locally replaced a `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` style `update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change` path with a small fused Triton kernel. This improved MTP1 n32 throughput from `1824.31 tok/s` to `1980.96 tok/s`, but it did not solve the full graph-mode overhead problem, especially for MTP2.

## Local experiments that were not safe enough to use

We also tried more aggressive local fast paths:

- a greedy rejection fast path for `temperature=0`
- packed/allfast variants
- faster attention metadata experiments
- GPU token cache / active request gating variants

Some of these either regressed performance or produced non-clean outputs such as `length:1` in offset tests, so we did not count them as valid benchmark results.

## Questions

1. Is it expected that Qwen native MTP in vLLM graph mode can be slower than no-MTP graph baseline even with MTP1 acceptance around `82%-88%`?
2. For `num_speculative_tokens > 1`, does vLLM currently run the same Qwen MTP layer multiple times / perform repeated per-token processing rather than producing multiple draft tokens in one low-overhead pass?
3. Are there known bottlenecks or planned optimizations for:
   - `reject_sample_kernel`
   - spec decode metadata preparation
   - slot mapping updates
   - `num_computed_tokens` correction/update
   - target/draft metadata reuse under CUDA graph
4. Is there a recommended benchmark setup for fairly comparing no-MTP graph baseline vs native MTP graph mode for long-output multimodal workloads?
5. Would the vLLM team be interested in a minimal repro using a public Qwen3.5 native-MTP checkpoint, if available, or local profiling traces from our private OCR checkpoint?

## Expected behavior

For a native MTP model with `80%+` MTP1 acceptance and graph mode enabled, we would expect MTP1 to at least be competitive with no-MTP graph baseline, or for documentation to clarify that MTP may be slower in graph mode unless the acceptance rate and sequence/batch shape meet specific thresholds.

For MTP2/MTP3, we would expect either:

- a low-overhead multi-token draft path, or
- guidance that `num_speculative_tokens > 1` may be slower for Qwen native MTP because it requires repeated MTP forward/processing.

## Actual behavior

On this workload:

- no-MTP graph baseline is still the fastest stable path.
- MTP1 has good acceptance but is slower end to end.
- MTP2 increases mean accepted length but introduces enough extra overhead that it still does not beat the best no-MTP graph baseline.
- Local profiling points to rejection sampling, metadata preparation, slot mapping, and `num_computed_tokens` updates as major overheads.

## Additional context

This benchmark is from a private OCR/document parsing workload, so some exact data/model paths are not public. We can prepare a smaller reproducer if a public Qwen native-MTP checkpoint is suitable.

The most relevant local observation is that the bottleneck is not just draft quality. Even when acceptance is usable, the spec decode path can be too expensive relative to a strong CUDA graph no-MTP baseline.

title: [Docs] Feedback for `/en/stable/serving/data_parallel_deployment/` load balancing with respect to vllm-router
body:
### 📚 The doc issue

In data parallel deployments, it is not well documented that vllm-router is capable to route requests to specific data-parallel engines within a vllm deployment via `--intra-node-data-parallel-size`.

This can effectively leverage session-affinity routing with data-parallel deployments in the presence of a conversational or agentic workload where a request's context is reused by the same client over and over.

### Suggest a potential alternative/fix

It does not fit well with the current load balancing classification (internal, hybrid, external) because it looks like this is specific to vllm-router, but it would be handy to explicitly mention that it is possible to route requests to specific engines within a single HTTP endpoint and demonstrate it with an example using `vllm-router --intra-node-data-parallel-size N`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: vLLM does not ignore temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty for DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, unlike the official DeepSeek API
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary According to the official DeepSeek API documentation, the DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode does not support the temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty parameters. For backward compatibility, passing these parameters does not raise an error, but they have no effect. However, vLLM does not behave consistently with the DeepSeek API. When serving DeepSeek V4 series models in thinking mode, these parameters are still applied to sampling instead of being ignored. Expected behavior For DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, vLLM should accept temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty without raising an error, but silently ignore them — matching the official DeepSeek API behavior. Actual behavior These parameters are still honored by the sampler, which can lead to different (and unexpected) outputs compared to the official API. Impact Users migrating from the official DeepSeek API to vLLM may get inconsistent results. Clients that rely on the documented "accepted but ignored" behavior may unintentionally change model output. Reproducibility across the official API and vLLM is broken for these models. Steps to reproduce Serve a DeepSeek V4 series model in thinking mode with vLLM. Send a request with different values of temperature (or presence_penalty / frequency_penalty). Observe that the output changes, whereas the official DeepSeek API would produce identical sampling behavior regardless of these values. Suggested fix Detect DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode and skip applying temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty in the sampling path, while still accepting them in the request schema for compatibility. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Feature/Design]: UVA weight offload on quantized MoE — pin_memory() power-of-two rounding wastes ~35% host RAM, and MXFP4 process_weights_after_loading silently un-offloads layers via replace_parameter
body:
## Summary

Two independent host-memory problems make `--offload-backend uva` on quantized MoE checkpoints fail at scales where the arithmetic says they should fit. Both were hit bringing up `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL` (1.02T, MXFP4 experts, 527 GiB on disk) on a single DGX Station GB300 (250 GiB HBM visible, 494 GiB Grace host RAM, coherent C2C). Both have working local patches; I'm opening this as a design question rather than a PR because the right fix touches `offloader/uva.py` and the quantization `process_weights_after_loading` contract, and maintainers should pick the shape.

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-d05da62e` (0.29.1rc1.dev422). Both code paths are unchanged on `main` as of today (`uva.py` L115 `cpu_data.pin_memory()`; `mxfp4.py` L358–361 `replace_parameter`).

## Problem 1: `pin_memory()` rounds every offloaded tensor up to a power of two

`UVAOffloader.wrap_modules` pins each offloaded parameter with `torch.Tensor.pin_memory()`, which goes through the CachingHostAllocator and rounds each allocation to the next power of two. For MiMo-Pro's per-layer expert tensors: `w13_weight` is 4.5 GiB → 8 GiB pinned, `w2_weight` 2.25 GiB → 4 GiB. Requesting `--cpu-offload-gb 305` consumed ~504 GiB of host memory and the kernel OOM-killed the EngineCore during load (host 494 GiB). Measured with a small probe that pins tensors of the real shapes and reads `Mlocked`/`Shmem` from `/proc/meminfo` before and after.

That's a ~33–45% host-RAM tax on exactly the workload UVA offload exists for, and it's invisible: the log reports "Total CPU offloaded parameters: 305 GiB" while the host holds far more.

**Local fix that works:** register the existing contiguous CPU tensor in place with `cudaHostRegister(ptr, nbytes, cudaHostRegisterPortable)` via ctypes (exact size), and keep a reference so it's never unregistered. With that, 321.75 GiB offloaded pins 321.75 GiB; the full model loads with 126 GiB host free. Read bandwidth through the resulting CUDA view was 336 GB/s vs 355 GB/s for the `pin_memory()` path on this box — a wash.

**Design question:** is an in-place `cudaHostRegister` path acceptable in `uva.py` (env-gated, or automatic above some size threshold), or would you rather expose a way to allocate exact-size pinned memory (e.g. `cudaHostAlloc` + `torch.from_blob`) so the caching allocator isn't involved at all? I can send either as a PR.

## Problem 2: `Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` un-offloads every layer via `replace_parameter`

On the Marlin/TRT-LLM MXFP4 path, `process_weights_after_loading` shuffles/re-packs the expert weights and installs the result with `replace_parameter(layer, "w13_weight", w13)` (and w2, and both scale tensors). `replace_parameter` registers the new tensor as a fresh `nn.Parameter`. The new tensor lives wherever the shuffle produced it (HBM), so the UVA view the offloader installed is dropped and the layer silently comes back onto the GPU: +7.17 GiB HBM per MoE layer on MiMo-Pro. With 46 of 69 MoE layers offloaded the box runs out of HBM after a handful of layers — the failure is a CUDA OOM inside `process_weights_after_loading`, nowhere near the offloader, so it's hard to attribute.

**Local fix that works:** when the existing parameter carries the offloader's `_vllm_is_uva_offloaded` marker and the new tensor has the same byte size, byte-copy the new contents into the existing pinned storage through a `uint8` view and re-view it to the new dtype/shape, preserving the UVA view; fall back to `replace_parameter` (with a warning) if the size changed. Verified: 5/5 greedy prompts token-exact between offloaded and non-offloaded runs of the same weights (8- and 16-layer truncations), and the full model serves correctly.

**Design question:** should `replace_parameter` itself become offload-aware (check the marker, copy in place), so every quant method benefits, or should quant methods that re-pack weights call a new helper? The former is one function; the latter is a per-backend audit (`mxfp4.py` is the one I hit; `fp8.py`, `nvfp4`, `compressed_tensors` likely have the same shape).

## Repro

```
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 320 \
  --cpu-offload-params routed_experts.w13_weight routed_experts.w2_weight \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96
```
Problem 1 shows as a host OOM-kill during load on a 494 GiB host; problem 2 shows as `torch.OutOfMemoryError` in `Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` once problem 1 is worked around. With both local patches this serves at 30 tok/s C1 / 56 tok/s aggregate at C8.

Write-up with per-boot receipts: https://al-engr.com/gb300-mimo-v26-pro-testing.html. Happy to send PRs once there's a preferred shape, and to test on this hardware.

title: [Feature]: Integer token IDs for logprobs in `/inference/v1/generate` responses (`GenerateLogProbs`)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Tracking issue for the `GenerateLogProbs` shape redesign. @sagearc raised it on #42729 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42729#issuecomment-4547904742).

#### The problem

`/inference/v1/generate` is a vLLM defined token in / token out API (#24261) but its output logprobs use an OpenAI shape. `GenerateResponseChoice.logprobs` and `GenerateResponseStreamChoice.logprobs` are `ChatCompletionLogProbs` where `token` is a string. The generate server has no tokenizer, so it writes every token as a `"token_id:N"` placeholder and derender parses the placeholders back out.

This causes a few problems:

- **The OpenAI shape leaks into a vLLM protocol.** Converting to OpenAI's string tokens belongs in derender (or the coupled chat / completions path), not on the generate server.
- **The format is an untyped string contract.** On the encoding side it's `_create_tokens_logprobs` in Python and `format_token_id` in the Rust frontend's `routes/inference/generate.rs`. On the decoding side it's `resolve_token_id_placeholder` and `_parse_token_id_placeholder`. Nothing in the schema says what `token` holds.
- **The two frontends already disagree on `bytes`.** Python leaves `bytes` unset. Rust sets it to the UTF-8 bytes of the placeholder itself (`"token_id:42"`). Derender overwrites it either way but a client reading generate directly gets different answers depending on the frontend.
- **One response, two shapes.** `prompt_logprobs` on the same `GenerateResponse` is already integer keyed (`list[dict[int, Logprob] | None]`). Output logprobs aren't.
- **Clients that want IDs have to parse strings.** A consumer reading generate directly (e.g. an RL rollout collector) gets top-k candidates only as placeholder strings. `rank` which the engine computes is dropped.

#### Proposal

A generate specific type with integer token IDs, for example:

```python
class GenerateLogProb(BaseModel):
    token_id: int
    logprob: float
    rank: int | None = None


class GenerateLogProbsContent(GenerateLogProb):
    top_logprobs: list[GenerateLogProb] = []


class GenerateLogProbs(BaseModel):
    content: list[GenerateLogProbsContent] | None = None
```

`content[i].logprob` and `content[i].top_logprobs[j].logprob` stay where they are today. `token` becomes `token_id` and `bytes` goes away. Derender converts this to `ChatCompletionLogProbs` / `CompletionLogProbs`, filling `token` and `bytes` from the tokenizer with the same U+FFFD correction it applies now (`_correct_decoded_token`). The placeholder parsing drops out of the generate → derender path.

`return_tokens_as_token_ids` on `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` is out of scope. It's a user facing OpenAI option that uses the `token_id:N` format on purpose.

Scope:

- Python `/inference/v1/generate` (`scale_out/token_in_token_out`), streaming and non-streaming
- Rust frontend `/inference/v1/generate` (`routes/inference/generate`)
- derender, batch and streaming (`OnlineDerenderer`)
- docs and a release note

#### Open questions

- **Compatibility.** Generate has direct consumers. I'd lean toward replacing the field in one release with a release note. The API is vLLM defined and with the shape above, code that reads only `content[i].logprob` keeps working. The other options are an opt in request field that flips default later or a second field next to the current one (see Alternatives).
- **`rank`.** Include it? It's cheap, the engine already has it and the Rust frontend's gRPC `CandidateTokenInfo` carries it.
- **List or dict for `top_logprobs`.** A list keeps rank order explicit and maps field for field onto the OpenAI shapes. A `dict[int, float]` is smaller but JSON turns the keys into strings.
- **#57442.** That PR adds `choices[].token_logprobs: list[float]` to `GenerateResponseChoice` as a fast path for sampled token logprobs. Generate would then have three logprob shapes: placeholder strings, integer keyed `prompt_logprobs` and a flat float list. We should decide together whether `token_logprobs` stays a separate field or becomes a mode of `GenerateLogProbs`.

#### Done when

- [ ] Shape and compatibility approach agreed here, coordinated with #57442
- [ ] Python and Rust `/inference/v1/generate` return the new shape, streaming and non-streaming
- [ ] Derender converts it to the OpenAI shapes on the batch and streaming paths. Existing logprob tests pass, including U+FFFD correction and `test_derender_parity.py` logprobs still match coupled serving
- [ ] Docs describe the generate logprob shape. Release note written

### Alternatives

- **Keep the placeholders and document them.** Cheapest option. The format becomes an explicit part of the protocol, but the types stay loose and the `bytes` mismatch stays.
- **Carry raw engine `Logprob` dicts, like `prompt_logprobs`.** Reuses a shape that's already on the wire and lets derender share `_create_chat_logprobs` with coupled serving. But `Logprob.decoded_token` can't be filled without a tokenizer (the Rust frontend puts the placeholder in it) and it ties the wire format to an internal engine type.
- **Add the integer shape as a second field** instead of replacing `logprobs`. Nothing breaks but there are two shapes on the wire and both get paid for if a client asks for both.

### Additional context

- @sagearc's comment: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42729#issuecomment-4547904742
- #42729 and #47161 "Out of scope" sections
- #24261: the tokens in / tokens out `/generate` endpoint
- #57442: `return_token_logprobs` fast path on generate
- #55029: streaming derender logprobs. It resolves placeholders per chunk and leaves this redesign deferred. Landing it first on the current shape is fine since this change only affects derender's input side.
- Code:
  - encoding: `vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py` (`_create_tokens_logprobs`), `rust/src/server/src/routes/inference/generate.rs` (`format_token_id`)
  - decoding: `vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py` (`_resolve_logprobs`), `vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py` (`resolve_token_id_placeholder`)

cc @sagearc @NickLucche @shimib @yinli-systems

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug `apply_softcap` in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_attention_helpers.py` computes `x * tanh(S / x)` as `x * (exp(S/x) - exp(-S/x)) / (exp(S/x) + exp(-S/x))`. Both exponentials overflow to `inf` when `|S / x| > ~88`, so the ratio is `inf / inf = NaN` and the whole attention row is poisoned. This path runs for models that use attention logit softcapping, for example Gemma-2 with `attn_logit_softcapping = 50`. A pre-softcap score above 4400 overflows. These models have very large attention logits, which is why they use softcapping. The same helper is used by the unified, DiffKV, and INT4 attention kernels. Reproduced on main at commit `c191787a68` with a GTX 1650 Ti and Triton 3.7.1. Reproduction: ```python import torch from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_attention_helpers import apply_softcap @triton.jit def _probe(s_ptr, out_ptr, n, cap, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) mask = offs < n s = tl.load(s_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0) tl.store(out_ptr + offs, apply_softcap(s, cap), mask=mask) cap = 50.0 s = torch.tensor( [1000.0, 3000.0, 5000.0, 10000.0, -10000.0, 4400.0], device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, ) out = torch.empty_like(s) _probe[(1,)](s, out, s.numel(), cap, BLOCK=16) print("kernel:", out.tolist()) print("tanh :", (cap * torch.tanh(s / cap)).tolist()) ``` Observed: ```text kernel: [50.0, 50.0, nan, nan, nan, inf] tanh : [50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, -50.0, 50.0] ``` Expected: the softcap returns a finite value, `x * tanh(S / x)`, for every finite score. A stable form is `x * (1 - 2 / (exp(2 * S / x) + 1))`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [RFC]: Request level text and derender output on `/inference/v1/generate`
body:
### Motivation.

The disaggregated serving path in vLLM is render → generate → derender. `/render` turns an OpenAI request into a `GenerateRequest` (#36166). `/inference/v1/generate` runs it on the GPU tier and returns token IDs (#22817, #24261).
`/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender` turn the result back into an OpenAI response (#42729).
This works well for batch and RL traffic where the caller already holds the complete `GenerateResponse`.

Latency sensitive interactive traffic in prefill/decode (P/D) deployments is a poor fit. Streaming derender (#47161) is a stateless per chunk translator, so every SSE chunk from generate costs the client another HTTP round trip:

- One `POST` per chunk with the client echoing `stream_state` back on each call.
- On the parsing path the full `chat_request` is re-sent with every chunk.
- Parser state is rebuilt by replaying all output tokens each chunk. #50550 documents this as O(n³) character work over a generation and defers caching it.

All of this lands on the TPOT critical path and for parsed output the cost grows with response length. A benchmark
of the streaming derender PRs measured it (1×A100-40G, Qwen3-8B, hermes + qwen3 parsers, main plus #50550, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033). At matched load, detokenize and parse on the derender tier cost ~9× the in-process CPU, and E2E p50 rose 15% on multi-thousand-token reasoning outputs. Tokens-in / text-out in a single call already works on the main server (`/v1/completions` accepts token IDs in `prompt`). The gap is specific to deployments whose wire format is `GenerateRequest`.

**Tokenizer availability is per pool. Detokenization is already per request.** Only one of these is a launch time decision:

| | Granularity | Where it's decided today |
|---|---|---|
| Tokenizer loaded | per pool, at launch | `--tokens-only` sets `skip_tokenizer_init` |
| Detokenize this request | per request | `SamplingParams.detokenize`, default `True`. `GenerateRequest.sampling_params` is a full `SamplingParams`, so it's on the wire today. |

The only thing that makes detokenization look launch level is `--tokens-only` overriding the request value. A generate server launched with `--enable-scale-out` and without `--tokens-only` already runs a `FastIncrementalDetokenizer` for every request. The handler then builds the response from `output.token_ids` only and throws `output.text` away.

**P/D makes request level the natural grain:**

- **Only the terminal leg's output reaches the client.** Proxies run the prefill leg with `max_tokens=1` and keep only `kv_transfer_params`. Decode recomputes the last prompt token to sample the first output token itself.
- **Decode already has everything detokenization needs.** `GenerateRequest.token_ids` carries the full prompt and the detokenizer primes its `DecodeStream` from it. No detokenizer state crosses the P→D boundary.
- **State lives with the live request.** `RequestState` owns the detokenizer and is popped on finish and on abort/disconnect. There's no session registry or eviction. That's the property #47161 couldn't get on the stateless derender tier which has no live request to hang state on.
- **No new pool flavor.** P/D fleets already run prefill and decode pools with different launch configs. Prefill pools stay `--tokens-only`. Decode pools load a tokenizer.

This also continues #22817's original design, which says *"We can make `Detokenization` step optional in the `AsyncLLM`"* and sketches a service mapping `GenerateRequest` → `ChatCompletionResponse`.

### Proposed Change.

#### 1. A request-level `output_mode` field

Add a top level field to `GenerateRequest`:

```python
output_mode: Literal["tokens", "text", "derender"] = "tokens"
```

It's a new field rather than a reuse of `sampling_params.detokenize`. That field defaults to `True`, so keying response content off it would change every existing response on tokenizer loaded servers. It's also an engine field and response shape is a serving concern.

| Level | Response adds | Equivalent today | Server needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tokens` (default) | nothing, unchanged behavior | `/inference/v1/generate` | nothing |
| `text` | detokenized `text`, resolved logprob tokens | `/v1/completions/derender` | tokenizer |
| `derender` | `content`, `reasoning`, `tool_calls` | `/v1/chat/completions/derender` | tokenizer, parser config, per request parser context |

#### 2. Response shape (proposed, see open question 1)

Keep the generate format and add optional fields that reuse existing OpenAI types:

```python
class GenerateResponseChoice(BaseModel):
    ...  # index, logprobs, finish_reason, token_ids, routed_experts, sampling_mask
    text: str | None = None             # output_mode="text"
    message: ChatMessage | None = None  # output_mode="derender"

class GenerateResponseStreamChoice(BaseModel):
    ...
    text: str | None = None             # output_mode="text", delta text
    delta: DeltaMessage | None = None   # output_mode="derender"
```

- One response schema for the endpoint regardless of mode. Generate only fields (`token_ids`, `routed_experts`, `sampling_mask`, `kv_transfer_params`) keep their place.
- `message` / `delta` are the same types `/derender` and `/v1/chat/completions` emit, so the parity check compares field for field.
- New fields are `None` and omitted unless requested, so existing clients see no change. Python generate doesn't omit absent fields on its own today: non-streaming responses use a plain `model_dump()` and stream chunks only exclude `prompt_token_ids`, `mm_placeholders` and `metrics` (#57264 switched to `exclude_none` and was reverted in #57302). So the implementation excludes `text`, `message` and `delta` explicitly when they're unset. The Rust frontend already omits absent fields.

Example decode-leg request and stream chunk:

```json
{"token_ids": [151644, 872, ...], "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 512},
 "stream": true, "output_mode": "text", "kv_transfer_params": {...}}
```

```json
{"request_id": "...", "choices": [{"index": 0, "token_ids": [9707], "text": " Hello"}]}
```

#### 3. Parser context for the `derender` level (proposed, see open question 2)

Parsers are built per request from context `GenerateRequest` doesn't carry today: `tools`, `tool_choice`, `chat_template_kwargs`. Batch `/derender` solves this by taking the post `adjust_request`
`ChatCompletionRequest`. The proposal mirrors it:

```python
chat_request: ChatCompletionRequest | None = None  # used only when output_mode="derender"
```

- It's sent once per request, not once per chunk as with streaming derender.
- It reuses the batch derender path (`OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat`) and its parity tests with stop string handling added (section 9). That path runs on the renderer's executor which has `renderer_num_workers` threads, default `1`. It runs once per request and decode pools do no prompt tokenization, so contention is low but the pool size caps concurrent `derender` calls.
- Without `chat_request`, a server with a reasoning or tool parser configured returns **400** (section 6). Batch `/derender` falls back to plain detokenization instead which can mix reasoning or tool call markup into `message.content`. Streaming derender already fails closed for parser configured models. Clients that want plain text use `text`. On a server with no parser, `derender` without `chat_request` puts the plain text in `message.content`.

#### 4. Streaming

- **`text`**: `text` carries each chunk's delta from the request's existing incremental detokenizer (`RequestOutputKind.DELTA`). No extra state.
- **`derender`**: one `Parser` per choice, created when the request starts and kept for its lifetime, the same way `/v1/chat/completions` streams today. There's no replay, no `stream_state` and no per chunk `chat_request`.
- **End of stream**: at `text` and `derender` levels, the stream emits a chunk whenever the engine output carries new text or a `finish_reason`, even with no new token IDs. That covers the final output the engine produces on `/abort_requests` which has no token IDs but can flush text held back for stop string matching. The generate stream skips outputs with no new token IDs today (on `main`, #53187 only keeps them while prompt metadata is pending), so `tokens` streams already drop a finish only chunk. #47933 (open) fixes that for `tokens` by emitting the terminal chunk when `finish_reason` is set. Phase 1 builds on it and also emits chunks that carry only new text.

#### 5. Logprobs

At `text` and `derender` levels, logprob entries carry decoded token strings and `bytes`, as `/derender` produces, instead of the `token_id:N` placeholders generate emits today. The tokens level shape follows #57574.

Dense logprobs are the expensive case. At `top_logprobs=20` the benchmark measured 355 µs per logprob-bearing token and 0.83 of a frontend core within 1.2× of the GPU's token rate. On a tokenizer loaded server that cost is already paid at the `tokens` level: `LogprobsProcessor` decodes every top-k token whenever `sampling_params.detokenize` is true and generate then discards the strings. Clients that want wide logprobs off the decode host send `output_mode="tokens"` with `detokenize: false` (which rules out `stop` strings) or use a `--tokens-only` pool. The Phase 1 docs should say so.

#### 6. Validation (fail loud)

- `output_mode != "tokens"` on a server without a tokenizer → **400**. Today's no-op detokenizer returns `""`, so a naive implementation would return empty text with a 200 for any request routed to a `--tokens-only` pool.
- `output_mode != "tokens"` with `sampling_params.detokenize` explicitly `false` → **400**.
- `chat_request` set without `output_mode="derender"` → **400**, rather than silently ignoring it.
- `output_mode="derender"` without `chat_request` on a server with a reasoning or tool parser configured → **400**, rather than falling back to plain text that may contain reasoning or tool call markup.

**Rollout note:** `GenerateRequest` is a plain pydantic `BaseModel`, so servers without this change ignore `output_mode` and return tokens only with a 200. Clients should check for `text` / `message` in the response.

#### 7. Role agnostic P/D usage

The field has no behavior tied to pod role or `kv_transfer_params`. The same decode pod may serve some requests decode only and others after a remote prefill, so role keyed behavior would differ across those paths. Orchestrators set `output_mode` and `chat_request` on the terminal leg only. If they reach a tokenizer free prefill pool anyway, the 400 above surfaces the misconfiguration.

For llm-d: the coordinator builds the prefill request from scratch, so it needs no change. The NIXL v2 sidecar reuses the client body for prefill and overrides a fixed set of fields (`stream`, token limits, `kv_transfer_params`). It would need to reset `output_mode` and drop `chat_request` on the prefill request, keeping both for decode. Resetting only `output_mode` leaves `chat_request` on a `tokens` request, which section 6 rejects.

#### 8. Decoupling `--tokens-only`

A decode pool needs the generate API surface *with* a tokenizer. `--tokens-only` currently does four jobs:

| Job | Where | Proposal |
|---|---|---|
| Skip tokenizer init | [arg_utils](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/engine/arg_utils.py#L2385-L2386) | keep |
| Force `detokenize=False` | [factories](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/factories.py#L61) → [serving](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py#L249-L250) | keep |
| Register `/abort_requests` | [api_router](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/api_router.py#L77) | also register when generate is served on a tokenizer loaded server (open question 4) |
| Imply scale-out endpoints | [factories](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/362a64b21d5038691c929521478b63dcb4828e58/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/factories.py#L73) | keep |

A decode pool then runs `--enable-scale-out` with a tokenizer and without `--tokens-only`.

#### 9. Parity and shared code

The inline path and `/derender` must produce identical output or clients get different text depending on deployment.

- Both go through the same `Parser` code, with no parallel copy.
- Extend the round-trip parity test (#48617, streaming added in #57922) to assert `generate(output_mode=X)` matches `derender(generate(output_mode="tokens"))` for `text` and `derender`, batch and streaming.
- Streaming derender drops logprobs on `main`, so the streaming logprob checks depend on #55029.
- **Stop strings.** Inline levels follow the engine's stop handling, like `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`: a matched stop string is cut from the text unless `include_stop_str_in_output` is set. Token IDs keep every generated token, so decoding them in `/derender` brings the stop string back, plus anything after it in the same token. For requests with `stop`, the test asserts inline output matches the coupled endpoint and that `/derender` output starts with the inline text and differs only after it. The `tokens` leg has to run on a tokenizer-loaded server, since `--tokens-only` rejects `stop` with a 400 (#57058). `OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat` re-decodes token IDs, so the Phase 2 inline path has to apply the stop truncation before parsing.
- **End of stream.** Tests cover a final chunk carrying only buffered text or only a `finish_reason`, including after `/abort_requests` (section 4).

#### 10. Rust frontend

The Rust frontend serves generate over HTTP and gRPC and both need the change. The protocol should be agreed here once and mirrored in both with the Rust frontend owners.

**HTTP.** `rust/src/server/src/routes/inference/generate/types.rs` mirrors `GenerateRequest` / `GenerateResponse`. It takes `output_mode`, `chat_request`, `text`, `message` and `delta` as specified in sections 1 to 4.

**gRPC.** `rust/proto/inference.proto` (`Inference.Generate` / `GenerateStream`, enabled with `--grpc-port`) already serves most of the `text` level. It accepts `token_ids` and `kv_transfer_params` and returns decoded `text` on every `SequenceOutput` because `ResponseOptions.output_text` defaults to `true`. That's the reverse of HTTP generate where `tokens` is the default. gRPC shapes responses with per-field `ResponseOptions` flags rather than one mode, so the levels map onto flags:

| Level | gRPC today | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | `output_text: false`, `output_token_ids: true` | none |
| `text` | `output_text: true` (default) | resolved logprob tokens |
| `derender` | not supported | `DerenderOptions` on `ResponseOptions`, `ParsedOutput` on `SequenceOutput` |

Proposed additions. All are new fields or messages, so they're wire compatible:

```proto
message ResponseOptions {
  ...
  // Set for the derender level. output_text stays independent.
  // Set it false to drop the raw text.
  optional DerenderOptions derender = 9;
}

message DerenderOptions {
  // Post-adjust_request ChatCompletionRequest (open question 2).
  google.protobuf.Struct chat_request = 1;
}

message SequenceOutput {
  ...
  // Set for the derender level. The full message in Generate, a delta in GenerateStream.
  optional ParsedOutput parsed = 11;
}

message ParsedOutput {
  optional string content = 1;
  optional string reasoning = 2;
  repeated ToolCall tool_calls = 3;
}

message ToolCall {
  uint32 index = 1;
  string id = 2;         // first delta for this index only when streaming
  string name = 3;       // first delta for this index only when streaming
  string arguments = 4;  // full JSON in Generate, a fragment in GenerateStream
}
```

- **Logprobs.** Sampled and candidate logprobs carry token IDs only. `CandidateTokenInfo.TokenInfo` already has `text = 4` and `token_bytes = 5` commented out. The `text` level fills them and adds the same for the sampled token, matching section 5.
- **Finish reason.** `FinishInfo.FinishReason` gains `TOOL_CALLS` for the `finish_reason` rewrite `/derender` does when tool calls were emitted.
- **Parser context.** `chat_request` travels as `google.protobuf.Struct`, the same way `kv_transfer_params` does, until open question 2 settles its shape.
- **Validation.** Section 6's 400s become `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The no-tokenizer case doesn't come up because the Rust frontend doesn't support `--tokens-only` or `--skip-tokenizer-init` yet and always loads a tokenizer.
- **Streaming.** `GenerateStream` stays server streaming. Parsing runs with the request, so the client has nothing to send after it and bidirectional streaming isn't needed (Alternatives, item 7). `GenerateStream` forwards every decoded event without filtering on new token IDs, so the end of stream gap in section 4 may not apply here. The section 9 tests should confirm it.
- **Parity.** The `derender` level on both Rust surfaces uses the Rust parsers in `rust/src/parser` and depends on the Rust `/derender` work, which has stalled: #53223 closed unmerged on 2026-09-17 and the draft follow-ups #53418 / #53419 haven't moved since 2026-09-10. The Rust `derender` level needs someone to pick that stack back up. The section 9 parity tests also run against the Rust frontend so Rust and Python produce the same output.
- **Release.** The proto change ships with a `vllm-proto` version bump in the same PR, checked by `cargo-semver-checks` (see `rust/proto/README.md`).
- **Out of scope.** `vllm serve --grpc` uses the external `smg-grpc-servicer` package with its own proto.

#### 11. Phasing

| Phase | Scope |
|---|---|
| 1 | `output_mode` field, `text` level (batch and streaming), logprob resolution, validation, `/abort_requests` decoupling, docs, latency benchmarks (section 12) |
| 2 | `derender` level, batch: `chat_request` context, `message` on the choice, reusing `OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat` |
| 3 | `derender` level, streaming: request-scoped parsers, `delta` on stream choices, parity CI extension, latency benchmarks (section 12) |
| — | Rust frontend mirror, tracked with the Rust frontend owners |

#### 12. Latency benchmarks

The CPU numbers above don't cover latency. The Phase 1 and Phase 3 PRs report TTFT and TPOT for:

- inline `text` / `derender` against generate plus streaming derender, across concurrency levels and response lengths.
- `tokens` requests on the same pod, with and without `text` or `derender` traffic mixed in.

#### Alternatives considered

1. **Streaming derender as-is (#47161).** Keeps the GPU tier tokenizer free but puts a round trip and echoed state on every chunk, plus replay for parsed output. It stays the right tool for stateless postprocessing (RL, batch, gateways that own postprocessing). This RFC complements it and doesn't replace it.
2. **The gateway composes generate + derender.** The per chunk hop moves from client to gateway rather than going away. Holding state in the gateway instead means reimplementing postprocessing there.
3. **Server-side derender sessions keyed by `request_id`.** Rejected in #47161 (Option B) over session lifecycle, eviction and memory. The derender tier has no live request to attach state to. The generate server does.
4. **Token IDs on `/v1/chat/completions`.** Chat has no token ID input (`messages` is required). Even with one, a render produced `GenerateRequest` carries resolved `SamplingParams` that don't map back onto OpenAI request fields
   without re-resolving and orchestrators on the generate format would have to run two wire formats.
5. **Run the coupled OpenAI server on decode pools.** Decode pods leave the generate protocol with the same
   two format problem as (4).
6. **Reuse `sampling_params.detokenize` as the switch.** It defaults to `True`, so every existing response on a
   tokenizer loaded server would grow text and token only clients would pay for detokenization by default.
7. **gRPC bidirectional streaming derender** (suggested by @andylolu2 on slack). The client opens one bidi stream to the derender tier, sends the parser context once, then forwards each generate chunk. The parser lives on the stream until it closes. That removes the echoed `stream_state`, the per chunk `chat_request` and replay. It also answers the lifecycle and eviction objections behind (3) because state lasts exactly as long as the stream. It doesn't remove the hop though. Every chunk still passes from the generate stream through the derender stream on the TPOT path and clients would need gRPC next to the HTTP generate format. If a derender replica fails mid stream, the parser state goes with it and the client has to reconnect and replay. A WebSocket would give the same stream lifetime on the HTTP stack. This complements the RFC rather than replacing it. It fits #57571 as an alternative to the parser cache for consumers that want a tokenizer free GPU tier.

#### Costs and risks

- **CPU on the decode host.** Detokenization and parsing run in the API server process, not the engine core. They don't block the scheduler but they use host CPU. `text` adds little on a tokenizer loaded server because detokenization already runs there today. Parsing and logprob resolution are the new work. In the benchmark, with the GPU saturated, the in-process frontend stayed under 0.25 of a core for chat, reasoning and tool-calling traffic (24–144 µs per token), at least 3.5× headroom over the GPU's token rate. That was one A100 and a faster GPU narrows the gap.
  `--api-server-count` scales the frontend if it becomes the limit. Dense logprobs are the exception (section 5). Opt-in per request bounds the cost to the traffic that asks for it.
- **Parser config drift.** Decode pools need the same `--reasoning-parser`, `--tool-call-parser` and `--enable-auto-tool-choice` as the render tier. That's the same obligation the derender tier already has.
- **Two call sites for postprocessing.** Mitigated by shared `Parser` code and the parity CI in section 9.
- **Security.** The inline path postprocesses engine produced tokens bounded by the request's resolved limits. It doesn't accept caller supplied output token IDs the way `/derender` does, so it doesn't need `/derender`'s explicit bounds checks. `chat_request` is caller supplied and needs the same validation as on the chat and derender endpoints.

#### Open questions

1. **Response shape.** An extended generate format with `text` / `message` / `delta` (proposed) or return `ChatCompletionResponse` / `ChatCompletionStreamResponse` directly for `output_mode="derender"`? The latter is a drop-in for existing `/derender` consumers but the endpoint's response schema would then depend on a request field and the generate only fields would need a home. *Feedback so far:*
   - @nilig supports extending the generate response format (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5692634586).
2. **Parser context.** Embed the post-`adjust_request` `chat_request` (proposed), or have `/render` emit a slim derender context (`tools`, `tool_choice`, `chat_template_kwargs`, plus `adjust_request`-derived state) that clients pass through? The slim form is smaller but first needs a settled answer to the open `adjust_request` question from #42729. *Feedback so far:*
   - #42729 now proposes re-running `adjust_request` on the derender side. Once that's settled it answers this one too.
3. **Naming.** `output_mode` with `tokens | text | derender`, or something else?
4. **`/abort_requests`.** Register it whenever generate is served, add a separate flag or leave it tied to `--tokens-only`? *Feedback so far:*
   - @nilig wants it whenever generate is served, including on decode pools that load a tokenizer (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5692634586).
   - #55521 adds a general `/abort_requests` on every `vllm serve` server, where an empty or missing `request_ids` aborts all in-flight requests. The scale-out route returns 400 for a missing `request_ids`. If #55521 lands, the two routes clash on `--tokens-only` servers and the semantics need to be reconciled. That would also answer this question.
5. **Completions shaped parsing.** Is `text` enough for completions shaped clients or does anyone need reasoning/tool parsing on completions? Parsing on `/v1/completions/derender` is chat-only today. *Feedback so far:*
   - @shimib's logprob-heavy traffic is completions shaped and needs `text` plus resolved logprobs, not parsing (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033).
   - #42729 records that completions don't parse, which matches @shimib's feedback. #57922 documented it in `derenderer.md`.

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@chaunceyjiang @DarkLight1337 @vMaroon @NickLucche @nilig @njhill @robertgshaw2-redhat @sagearc @BugenZhao

### Any Other Things.

**Related work**
- #47161 / #50550: streaming derender and its parse path. Complementary to this RFC (Alternatives, item 1).
- #47313: adds `stop_reason` to generate response choices. It touches the same protocol and serving files, and the matched stop string would let `/derender` cut its text there too (section 9).
- #36983 / #51641: `delta_text` and `delta_token_ids` desync when stop strings are buffered. Streaming `text` inherits this and should use the fix.
- #53223 / #53418 / #53419: Rust `/derender` endpoints. #53223 closed unmerged and the drafts have stalled (section 10).
- #47933: emits the terminal `finish_reason` chunk on `tokens` streams, including after an abort (section 4).
- #55029: resolved logprobs on streaming derender chunks. The streaming logprob parity checks in section 9 need it.

**Related bug: #57052.** Stop strings break on the scale-out token path in two ways. On `--tokens-only` servers `stop` was silently ignored and generation ran to EOS or `max_tokens` with a 200. #57058 fixed that and the server now returns 400. On the derender side the stop text leaks back into the output because `/derender` re-decodes every token ID (section 9). That part is still open. Once decode pools run with a tokenizer, `stop` works there too.

**Out of scope**
- Skipping detokenization for `output_mode="tokens"` on tokenizer loaded servers where today it runs and its output is discarded. It's a worthwhile performance follow up but it changes existing behavior (`stop` strings need detok).
- Any change to `/derender` itself.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

## Bug description When using `vllm-0.23.1rc1.dev207`, tool call requests to the `/v1/responses` endpoint fail when using Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B with MTP enabled via `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp", "num_speculative_tokens":2}'`. The same requests complete successfully when `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp", "num_speculative_tokens":2}'` is removed from the start command. ~The issue appears to have been introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45413.~ ~Tagging the original author for visibility - @bbrowning~ Reverting back to v0.23.0 fixes the issue. ## Reproduction The bug can be reproduced using the responses api tool calling example from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/tool_calling/openai_responses_client_with_tools.py ```python # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project """ Set up this example by starting a vLLM OpenAI-compatible server with tool call options enabled. Reasoning models can be used through the Responses API as seen here https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses For example: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --structured-outputs-config.backend xgrammar \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes """ import json from openai import OpenAI def get_weather(latitude: float, longitude: float) -> str: """ Mock function to simulate getting weather data. In a real application, this would call an external weather API. """ return f"Current temperature at ({latitude}, {longitude}) is 20°C." tools = [ { "type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get current temperature for provided coordinates in celsius.", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "latitude": {"type": "number"}, "longitude": {"type": "number"}, }, "required": ["latitude", "longitude"], "additionalProperties": False, }, "strict": True, } ] input_messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather like in Paris today?"} ] def main(): base_url = "http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1" client = OpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key="empty") model = client.models.list().data[0].id response = client.responses.create( model=model, input=input_messages, tools=tools, tool_choice="required" ) for out in response.output: if out.type == "function_call": print("Function call:", out.name, out.arguments) tool_call = out args = json.loads(tool_call.arguments) result = get_weather(args["latitude"], args["longitude"]) input_messages.append(tool_call) # append model's function call message input_messages.append( { # append result message "type": "function_call_output", "call_id": tool_call.call_id, "output": str(result), } ) response_2 = client.responses.create( model=model, input=input_messages, tools=tools, ) print(response_2.output_text) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ## Output ```text (APIServer pid=109814) INFO: 127.0.0.1:43102 - "GET /v1/models HTTP/1.1" 200 OK (EngineCore pid=110013) ERROR 06-20 20:06:01 [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request resp_84efa6e4b1a854cb_0-adba64b9 for tokens 198. title: [Bug]: DiffusionGemma: tensor shape mismatch in post_norm under concurrent decode (inputs_embeds vs silently-clamped sc_embeds)
body:
### Summary

Both the NVFP4 and bf16 checkpoints of DiffusionGemma-26B-A4B crash the vLLM engine under concurrent request load, with the identical error:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (257) must match the size of tensor b (256) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

raised from `self.post_norm(inputs_embeds + sc_signal)` in `DiffusionGemmaSelfConditioning.forward()`. This kills the engine core process (`EngineDeadError` propagates to the API layer). It is **not deterministic at any fixed concurrency level** — across 4 independent runs (2 per checkpoint) it triggered at 4, 6, 6, and 16 concurrent users respectively, and never at 2 concurrent users.

This looks related to #50699 (same file, same "concurrent decode" trigger condition) but is a distinct bug — it reproduces at `--max-num-seqs 4`, well below the concurrency level where that issue's OOM appears, and the failure mode is a shape mismatch, not OOM.

### Root cause (traced to source)

Pulled `vllm/model_executor/models/diffusion_gemma.py` from the `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1` image. The crash site is `DiffusionGemmaModelState._apply_self_conditioning`:

```python
for slot, idx in zip(decode_slots_np.tolist(), decode_idx_np.tolist()):
    start = int(query_start_loc_np[idx])
    end = int(query_start_loc_np[idx + 1])
    canvas = slice(start, end)
    soft = sc_embeds[slot, : end - start]
    inputs_embeds[canvas] = self.model.self_conditioning(
        inputs_embeds[canvas], soft.to(inputs_embeds.dtype)
    )
```

- `inputs_embeds[canvas]` slices from `_inputs_embeds_buf`, a large batch-wide buffer — `inputs_embeds[start:end]` with `end - start = 257` legitimately returns 257 rows.
- `soft = sc_embeds[slot, :end - start]` slices from `self.diffusion_states.self_conditioning_embeds`, a **fixed-size per-slot buffer** shaped `[max_num_reqs, canvas_length, hidden_size]` where `canvas_length=256` for this checkpoint. PyTorch tensor slicing past the end of a dimension does not raise — it silently clamps. `sc_embeds[slot, :257]` on a 256-length dim quietly returns 256 rows.

Net effect: `inputs_embeds[canvas]` has 257 rows, `soft` is silently clamped to 256, both get passed into `self_conditioning.forward()` → `post_norm(inputs_embeds + sc_signal)` → shape mismatch, every time, with exactly these numbers.

**Open question**: why `end - start` (from `query_start_loc_np`, vLLM's scheduler output) is 257 instead of ≤ `canvas_length` for some request in some batches — that span computation lives in the scheduler, outside this file, and I haven't traced it further. This would explain why it only appears under concurrent/continuous-batched decode and never at single-request concurrency.

### Environment

- vLLM: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1`, torch `2.11.0+cu130`, CUDA `13.0`
- GPU: NVIDIA GB10 (unified memory), driver `580.142`, 1x GPU, `--tensor-parallel-size 1`
- Attention backend forced to `TRITON_ATTN` (heterogeneous head dims — `head_dim=256`, `global_head_dim=512` — make FA4 unavailable)
- `--enforce-eager`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3`, `enable_chunked_prefill=True`, `enable_prefix_caching=True`

NVFP4:
```
--model nvidia/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4
--quantization modelopt_fp4 --moe-backend marlin --reasoning-parser gemma4
--max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --enforce-eager
```

bf16:
```
--model google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it
--moe-backend triton --reasoning-parser gemma4
--max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.55 --enforce-eager
```

### Reproduction

Locust-based staged concurrency ramp (2 → 4 → 6 → 8 → 12 → 16 → 24 → 32 → 40 → 60 → 80 → 100 → 150 → 200 concurrent users, 150s/stage) against `/v1/chat/completions`, mixed plain-chat and RAG-augmented traffic.

| Run | Checkpoint | Crashed at (concurrent users) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | NVFP4 | 4 |
| 2 | NVFP4 | 6 |
| 3 | bf16  | 6 |
| 4 | bf16  | 16 |

### Observed (identical across all 4 runs)

```
(EngineCore pid=N) ERROR [core.py:1233]     return self.post_norm(inputs_embeds + sc_signal)
(EngineCore pid=N) ERROR [core.py:1233]                           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~
(EngineCore pid=N) ERROR [core.py:1233] RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (257) must match the size of tensor b (256) at non-singleton dimension 0
(APIServer pid=1) ERROR [async_llm.py:704] AsyncLLM output_handler failed.
(APIServer pid=1) ERROR [async_llm.py:704] Traceback (most recent call last):
(APIServer pid=1) ERROR [async_llm.py:704]   File ".../vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py", line 660, in output_handler
(APIServer pid=1) ERROR [async_llm.py:704]     outputs = await engine_core.get_output_async()
(APIServer pid=1) ERROR [async_llm.py:704]   File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py", line 1061, in get_output_async
(APIServer pid=1) ERROR [async_llm.py:704]     raise self._format_exception(outputs) from None
(APIServer pid=1) ERROR [async_llm.py:704] vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
```

### Not yet tried

- `--max-num-seqs 1`: should be decisive — if it never crashes at 1, confirms the span-boundary issue is specific to concurrent/continuous-batched scheduling.
- Disabling `--enable-chunked-prefill` / `--enable-prefix-caching` individually.
- A defensive clamp/assert on `end - start <= canvas_length` before the `sc_embeds` slice, so this fails loudly/predictably instead of silently truncating and crashing downstream, while the scheduler-side span computation gets root-caused separately.

Happy to help test a fix against our hardware if useful.

---

*Disclosure: this investigation (load testing, log analysis, and source tracing) was done with AI assistance (Claude Code), verified against real crashes on our own hardware (4 independent reproductions, full tracebacks and source excerpts above are from our own runs, not fabricated).*

title: [Usage]: Gemma4 on Turing GPUs (SM 7.5): all attention backends hit shared memory limits
body:
### Your current environment

```text
use the builtin dockerfile to build & manually install transformers==5.5.0
```


### How would you like to use vllm

# Summary

I'd like to share a compatibility finding for awareness: **Gemma4 models cannot currently run on Turing architecture GPUs (SM 7.5, e.g. RTX 2080 Ti) via any available attention backend in vLLM** by default. I understand this is likely an edge case given the age of the hardware, but wanted to document the situation in case it's useful for the project — either for improving error messaging or for considering potential kernel tuning.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| **vLLM version** | `0.19.1rc1.dev4` |
| **Commit** | [`fa9e680`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/fa9e68022d29c5396dfbb96d13587b6bc1bdb933) |
| **GPU** | 2× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti (22 GB, CC 7.5, Turing) |
| **CUDA Driver** | 580.126.18, CUDA 13.0 |
| **Python** | 3.12 (Docker) |
| **Model** | Gemma4-31B AWQ 4-bit (`google/gemma-4-31b-it`), also reproduced with `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` |

## What happens

Gemma4's `text_config` specifies `head_dim: 256` (sliding attention) and `global_head_dim: 512` (full attention). This large head dimension causes Triton-based attention kernels to require **96 KB shared memory**, but Turing GPUs have a hardware ceiling of **64 KB per SM**. Meanwhile, non-Triton backends are blocked by other constraints.

Here is the status of each backend I tested:

| Backend | Stage | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `FLASH_ATTN` | Startup (auto-excluded) | Requires SM ≥ 8.0; not available on Turing. |
| `FLASHINFER` | Startup | `Reason: ['head_size not supported']` — supports `[64, 128, 256]` only ([`flashinfer.py#L388-L390`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa9e68022d/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py#L388-L390)), Gemma4 full-attn layers need 512. |
| `TRITON_ATTN` | First inference | `OutOfResources: shared memory, Required: 98304, Hardware limit: 65536` — kernel at [`triton_unified_attention.py#L1124`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa9e68022d/vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py#L1124). |
| `FLEX_ATTENTION` | CUDA graph warmup | Same shared memory error via Inductor-generated Triton kernel (`triton_tem_fused_flex_attention_0`). |

## Reproduction

```bash
# With --attention-backend auto (default), TRITON_ATTN is selected;
# server starts but crashes on first request.
vllm serve /models \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype float16 \
  --max-model-len 32768

# Explicitly trying each backend:
vllm serve /models ... --attention-backend FLASHINFER    # fails at startup
vllm serve /models ... --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN   # fails on first request
vllm serve /models ... --attention-backend FLEX_ATTENTION # fails during warmup
```

## Relevant code paths

- **Backend auto-selection (CC < 10)**: [`cuda.py#L136-L141`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa9e68022d/vllm/platforms/cuda.py#L136-L141) — priority `FLASH_ATTN → FLASHINFER → TRITON_ATTN → FLEX_ATTENTION`
- **Backend validation & error raise**: [`cuda.py#L287-L300`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa9e68022d/vllm/platforms/cuda.py#L287-L300)
- **Triton kernel launch**: [`triton_unified_attention.py#L1124-L1155`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa9e68022d/vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py#L1124-L1155)
- **FlashInfer head_size list**: [`flashinfer.py#L388-L390`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa9e68022d/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py#L388-L390)
- **General backend validation**: [`backend.py#L268-L329`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa9e68022d/vllm/v1/attention/backend.py#L268-L329)
- **Gemma4 head_dim selection**: [`gemma4.py#L442-L445`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa9e68022d/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4.py#L442-L445)

## Suggestions (non-blocking, just ideas)

1. **Better early detection**: When *all* backends are invalid for a model+GPU combination, the current behavior with `TRITON_ATTN` is to start successfully but crash on the first request. An early check correlating `head_dim` with the GPU's shared memory capacity could provide a clearer error at startup.

2. **Smaller tiles for large head_dim**: In `triton_unified_attention.py`, reducing `TILE_SIZE` (e.g., from 32 to 16) for large `head_dim` on shared-memory-constrained GPUs could potentially bring usage below 64 KB, though this may impact performance.

3. **Documentation note**: It might be helpful to note in the Gemma4 model card or vLLM docs that CC 7.5 GPUs are not supported for this model family due to the large head dimension.

## Error logs

<details>
<summary>TRITON_ATTN (crashes on first request)</summary>

```
(Worker_TP0 pid=215) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:949]
  File ".../vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py", line 1124, in unified_attention
    kernel_unified_attention_2d[...]
  ...
triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory,
  Required: 98304, Hardware limit: 65536.
  Reducing block sizes or `num_stages` may help.
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>FLASHINFER (fails at startup)</summary>

```
(Worker_TP0 pid=215) ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER
  is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['head_size not supported']
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>FLEX_ATTENTION (fails during CUDA graph warmup)</summary>

```
(Worker_TP1 pid=216) torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: RuntimeError:
  No valid triton configs. OutOfMemoryError: out of resource:
  triton_tem_fused_flex_attention_0 Required: 98304 Hardware limit:65536
  Reducing block sizes or `num_stages` may help.
```

</details>

title: [Feature]: Add a built-in JSON logging formatter
body:
## Problem

vLLM can emit structured JSON logs today, but users must author and mount a
complete Python `logging.config.dictConfig` file and pass it with
`--logging-config.pylogging_config_file`. That is disproportionate when the
only desired change is to replace vLLM's default human-readable formatter with
JSON.

The typed `LoggingConfig` introduced by #57200 and #57205 provides the right
configuration surface, and #57955/#57957 make worker process metadata
compatible with valid JSON output. A simple built-in JSON choice is still
missing.

## Proposed solution

Add a `formatter` field to `LoggingConfig` with two initial values:

- `text` (default): retain the existing newline/color-aware formatters.
- `json`: replace the built-in text formatters with the bundled
  `python-json-logger` formatter.

Users could enable it through the existing configuration forms:

```bash
vllm serve MODEL --logging-config.formatter json
vllm serve MODEL --logging-config '{"formatter":"json"}'
```

The same field would work through serve YAML and Python configuration. The JSON
profile should include `asctime`, `levelname`, `name`, `vllm_process_name`,
`process`, and `message`. A user-supplied `pylogging_config_file` remains
authoritative and replaces the built-in configuration rather than being merged
with it.

This profile covers records emitted through vLLM's Python loggers. It does not
define an OpenTelemetry Logs Data Model schema, reconfigure Uvicorn, or convert
direct third-party/native writes to `stdout` or `stderr`.

## Prior efforts and non-duplication

- #32761 is the closest prior implementation of plain JSON logging. It predates
  `LoggingConfig`, uses an environment-variable switch and a custom formatter
  and exception hook, and is currently stale/conflicted. This proposal is
  materially different: it extends the typed configuration model and reuses
  the already bundled and documented `python-json-logger` formatter.
- #54769 proposes an OpenTelemetry-aligned JSON schema, trace/span correlation,
  and `VLLM_LOGGING_FORMAT`. That is a distinct profile and broader scope than
  the plain Python `LogRecord` JSON profile proposed here.
- #57200 defines the typed console-logging model and identifies a built-in JSON
  format as follow-up work; #57205 implements the initial model.
- #57955 and #57957 ensure process decoration does not corrupt JSON and expose
  the logical process name as structured metadata, but users still need to
  provide a complete logging configuration.
- #2397, #2432, and #13920 are earlier requests or implementations in this
  space.

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing users retain the current text output by default.
- `--logging-config.formatter json` emits one parseable JSON object per vLLM
  `LogRecord` with logical process name and PID fields.
- The selection propagates through `LoggingConfig` to child processes.
- A custom `pylogging_config_file` remains authoritative.
- CLI parsing, formatter output, default behavior, and documentation are
  covered by tests.

---

_Prepared with assistance from OpenAI Codex._
