title: [Bug]: v0.30 dependencies raise the effective compiler floor above GCC 11.3
body:
## Summary

vLLM v0.30.0's declared source-build floor remains GCC/G++ >= 11.3, but multiple pinned dependencies now require C++20 `<format>` / `std::format`. With libstdc++, that raises the effective GCC floor to GCC 13.

This is broader than the first observed DeepSelect failure: the DeepGEMM revision pinned by v0.30.0 independently uses `<format>` in host code that is included unconditionally when building its Python extension.

## Declared vLLM contract

vLLM both enforces GCC >= 11.3 and recommends installing GCC 11 on Ubuntu 22.04:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/CMakeLists.txt#L23-L29
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.cuda.inc.md#L140-L149

## DeepSelect: first observed failure

vLLM pins DeepSelect commit `d96d33afe1fab0d6066da49cdc91e64c2bee65ea`:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/cmake/external_projects/deepselect.cmake#L19-L22

That revision includes `<format>` and uses `std::format` once to construct a stride-validation error message:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepSelect/blob/d96d33afe1fab0d6066da49cdc91e64c2bee65ea/csrc/api.cpp#L15-L19
- https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepSelect/blob/d96d33afe1fab0d6066da49cdc91e64c2bee65ea/csrc/api.cpp#L89-L97

With GCC 11.4 and `-std=c++20`, compilation stops at:

```text
csrc/api.cpp:17:10: fatal error: format: No such file or directory
   17 | #include <format>
      |          ^~~~~~~~
```

Root-upstream tracking and the proposed portable replacement are available here:

- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect/issues/21
- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect/pull/22

## DeepGEMM: independent compiler-floor drift

vLLM v0.30.0 pins `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` commit `e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f`:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake#L30-L36

That exact pinned tree also requires `<format>`:

- `csrc/apis/attention.hpp` includes `<format>`, includes the SM100 sparse-MQA implementation, and uses `std::format`:
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/apis/attention.hpp#L1-L15
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/apis/attention.hpp#L64-L67
- `csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm100_sparse_mqa_logits.hpp` includes `<format>` and uses `std::format` repeatedly to construct JIT source:
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm100_sparse_mqa_logits.hpp#L1-L9
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm100_sparse_mqa_logits.hpp#L82-L109
- `csrc/python_api.cpp` includes `apis/attention.hpp` unconditionally, so runtime architecture gating does not prevent the host compiler from parsing this code:
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/csrc/python_api.cpp#L1-L15

DeepGEMM's own current requirements explicitly call for "Compilers and standard libraries with C++20 `<format>` support":

- https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/blob/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f/README.md#L24-L33

This source path did not produce the observed CI failure only because Ninja stopped after the earlier DeepSelect error. The pinned source and unconditional include chain show that fixing DeepSelect alone is insufficient for a GCC 11 build.

## What changed from v0.29.0

The known-good v0.29.0 build used GCC 11.4. Its DeepGEMM integration pinned the older `deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM` revision `8b1392b978f5a03c828dd1711090d7fb50958b8a`, before the linked sparse-MQA `<format>` code was present. DeepSelect was introduced in v0.30.0 as a new extension.

- v0.29.0 DeepGEMM pin: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake#L30-L34
- Known-good GCC 11.4 build: https://github.com/neuralmagic/nm-cicd/actions/runs/34346952915
- Failing v0.30.0 build: https://github.com/neuralmagic/nm-cicd/actions/runs/35729206971

## Compatibility decision needed

vLLM should make the declared and effective build contracts agree. The main options are:

1. Preserve GCC 11.3 compatibility by replacing or conditionally excluding incompatible `<format>` usage in all pinned host dependencies, then validate the minimum compiler in CI.
2. Intentionally raise the source-build requirement to a compiler and standard library with C++20 `<format>` support (GCC 13 for libstdc++), update the CMake guard and installation documentation, and validate that new floor in CI.

The DeepSelect PR above is still a useful portability fix, but it addresses only the first failure and does not resolve DeepGEMM's independent requirement.

title: [Bug][ROCm][Attention][KV Connector] DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x DSA sparse-MLA decode is garbage under CUDA graphs in PD-disaggregation (remote-prefilled KV)
body:
## Summary
In PD-disaggregated serving on ROCm/MI300X (MoRIIO KV connector, WideEP DP8/EP8), the **decode** engine emits degenerate repeated-token garbage (`locklocklock…` / `!!!`) for **remote-prefilled** requests whenever decode runs under **any CUDA-graph capture** (`FULL`, `PIECEWISE`, or `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`). With `DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager) the identical stack decodes **coherently**. Colocated (non-disagg) serving and vLLM v0.27.1 are unaffected.

## Environment
- vLLM **0.28.0** (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.28.0`), AITER 0.1.19, ROCm 7.2.3
- 2× **MI300X (gfx942)**, RoCEv2; KV connector = **MoRIIOConnector** (WRITE mode), `block_size=1`, fp8 KV
- Models: **GLM-5.3-FP8** and **GLM-5.1-FP8** (both `GlmMoeDsa`, DeepSeek-V3.2-style **DSA sparse-MLA**)
- Topology: 1P1D **WideEP DP8/EP8**; MTP on or off (does not matter)

## How to reproduce
1. Launch 1P1D PD-disagg (MoRIIO WRITE) — e.g. the AMD harness `.buildkite/amd-disagg/run-slurm-disagg-test.sh` with `WIDE_EP_MODE=1 MORIIO_READ_MODE=0` — using `DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`.
2. Send any request → decode returns `locklocklock…` (garbage).
3. Set `DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager) → decode is coherent. (`FULL` and `PIECEWISE` are each garbage too.)

## Expected behavior
Decode under CUDA graphs produces the same coherent output as eager decode (and as colocated single-node / vLLM v0.27.1).

## Isolation — what did NOT fix it vs what WORKED
We walked the full transfer→decode path with per-step, on-device instrumentation applied identically to both engines.

**Did NOT fix it (still garbage), i.e. ruled out as the cause:**
- **KV-cache content / transfer** — the transfer is complete and **bit-exact** (producer == consumer bytes for every layer, including the sparse-indexer k_cache). Explicitly transferring the indexer k_cache changed nothing.
- **MoRI library version** — swapping v1.1.0 ↔ commit `42e895472b08` (the version used by the working v0.27.1 recipe) made no difference.
- **MoRI-EP `combine()` fix** (#56073 / ROCm/mori#475) — inert here (our EP8 runs the single-node **IntraNode** combine, not the InterNodeV1 path that fix targets).
- **Decode metadata** — byte-identical local-vs-remote for the same prompt (`num_computed_tokens`, positions, seq_len, block_table, indexer top-k, and post-remap global KV slots all match). Nothing to correct.
- **KV dtype** — reproduces with **fp8 and bf16** (so not an fp8-scale/dequant issue).
- **Transfer mode** — reproduces in **both READ and WRITE** MoRIIO modes.
- **MTP** — reproduces with speculative decode **on and off**.
- **Widening the eager CUDA-graph region** — restoring a broad `eager_break_during_capture` over the whole sparse decode (breakable/PIECEWISE) **still produced garbage**.

**WORKED (coherent), i.e. the differentiators:**
- **`DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager decode)** — coherent, 3/3 prompts, MTP on and off.
- **Colocated single-node DP8/EP8** on the *same* v0.28 build/kernels/model (no remote KV) — coherent.
- **vLLM v0.27.1 + WideEP overlay** — the *same* PD-disagg path decodes coherently.

→ Coherent vs garbage turns on exactly **two conditions being simultaneously true: (1) the DSA sparse-MLA decode is captured in a CUDA graph, AND (2) it is consuming remotely-populated KV.** Removing *either* — run decode eager, or serve the same request colocated (locally-populated KV) — restores coherence. Reproduces on ≥2 DSA models (GLM-5.3-FP8, GLM-5.1-FP8). The corruption therefore lives in the **CUDA-graph capture/replay × remotely-populated-KV buffer lifecycle** of the DSA sparse-MLA decode (replayed steps appear to read stale sparse-index / remote-KV state), and it is **not** in transfer, metadata, scales, dtype, mode, MTP, or the eager-region width.

## Possibly related — and why
- **#51425 "[Perf] Narrow DeepSeek V3.2 eager CUDA graph region"** — the most direct link. It moved most of the DSA attention (query prep, norm/RoPE, GEMMs) *out* of the eager break and *into* the captured graph, leaving only `_sparse_indexer_and_attn` eager. This is the v0.28 change that first placed per-step DSA sparse-decode state under CUDA-graph capture, and GLM-5.x (DeepSeek-V3.2 architecture) rides exactly this path.
- **#51430 / #51768 / #52401 (DeepSeek-V4 analog)** — strong precedent that this class silently corrupts. #51430 applied the same narrowing to V4; #51768 then documented that **V4 + Model-Runner-V1 + PIECEWISE/FULL_AND_PIECEWISE = silent output corruption** and rejected that combo, noting **eager/NONE** as the mitigation (exactly our workaround); #52401 fixed it by choosing the eager region **per model runner**. So the fix pattern exists — but it was applied to **V4 only**, not to **V3.2 / GLM-5.x**, and not to the **PD-disagg remote-KV** case.
- **#56726 "[ROCm][Bugfix] Ignore descales for unquantized AITER caches"** — same *failure shape*: an AITER decode kernel consuming a **stale/unused scale (descale) tensor** corrupts output, and it surfaces under **CUDA-graph recapture**. Our MLA decode kernel is invoked as `mla_decode_fwd(q_scale=_q_scale, kv_scale=_k_scale)` — the direct analog; if those descales are captured stale, it matches our capture-only, dtype-independent signature. (#56726 patches the FA backend for *unquantized* caches, so it is not a drop-in fix for our MLA-sparse/fp8 path, but the mechanism is the same.)

**Why the existing fixes don't cover us:** widening the eager region (the #52401-style broad eager break over the sparse decode) **did not** restore coherence in our repro — so the corrupting operation is in a segment that stays captured even under the broad eager region. The residual defect is the **CUDA-graph × remotely-populated-KV buffer lifecycle**, which is deeper than eager-region width alone and specific to the PD-disagg (remote-prefill) decode path that none of the above PRs exercised.

## Workaround
`DECODE_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE` (eager decode) — coherent, but ~5–8× slower decode throughput.

<sub>Investigation/repro assisted by AI tools; results reviewed and validated on-cluster.</sub>

title: [Feature]: Parser cache for streaming chat derender and stable tool call IDs on retried calls
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Tracking issue for work deferred from the streaming derender RFC #47161 and PR #50550: server side parser state for streaming chat derender, and keeping tool call IDs stable when a chunk is retried.

#### Where things stand

With a reasoning or tool parser configured, streaming chat derender keeps nothing on the server. Each chunk builds a fresh parser, replays the history the client echoes back in `stream_state` (`output_token_ids`, split by `output_chunk_lens`) through `parse_delta`, then feeds the new chunk (`OnlineDerenderer._derender_chat_stream_parsed`). Any replica can serve any chunk and the client carried state is the only source of truth.

The price is replay. It's O(n²) `parse_delta` calls over a generation and O(n³) character work for parsers that re-scan accumulated text (Hermes tool call JSON, DeepSeek-R1 reasoning). The "Streaming cost" section of `derenderer.md` documents this. @shimib measured it on 1×A100-40G with Qwen3-8B and the hermes + qwen3 parsers (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033): ~9× the in-process CPU at matched load, +15% E2E p50 on multi-thousand-token reasoning outputs and a saturated tier under concurrent parsed streams with the default `renderer_num_workers=1`.

Latency sensitive P/D goes to #56851 where the parser lives with the request on the decode pool and there's no replay. This issue covers the consumers that keep using streaming derender: RL, batch and gateways that own postprocessing.

#### 1. Parser cache

An LRU of live `Parser` instances on the derenderer, keyed by `(request_id, choice_index)`, as the "Future" note in #47161 describes. Each entry records how many chunks its parser has consumed. On a hit where that matches `len(stream_state.output_chunk_lens)`, skip replay and feed only the new chunk, so compute drops to O(delta). Anything else falls back to full replay: first chunk, eviction, a chunk that landed on another replica, a retry or out of order input. `stream_state` stays authoritative, so there's no protocol change and a hit has to produce exactly what replay would.

Design questions:

- **What a hit must check.** `request_id` comes from the client (`generate_chunk.request_id`), so the key alone can't be trusted. A hit needs to confirm the cached parser saw the same `prompt_token_ids`, `chat_request` and output history, e.g. with a digest stored in the entry. Otherwise one stream can pick up another stream's parser state.
- **Memory bounds and eviction.** Bound by entry count and TTL, and evict on the finish chunk. Streams abandoned midway never send a finish chunk, so the TTL has to cover them.
- **Concurrency.** Parsing runs on the renderer executor's thread pool and a retry can race the original call. Taking the entry out of the cache for the duration of the call and putting it back at its new position keeps two calls from sharing a parser.
- **Routing.** Without session affinity, a stream's chunks spread across N replicas and the hit rate drops to about 1/N. We should document routing on `request_id` for deployments that want the cache to pay off.
- **Default.** I'd make it opt in and off by default, so a stateless render tier stays the default.
- **What to cache.** A bare `Parser` or the shared per choice `ChatStreamProcessor` (#57572) if that lands first.

#### 2. Tool call ID stability on retried calls

Raised by @sagearc in the #50550 review (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913963783).

Within one stream, IDs are already stable. `stream_state.last_tool_call_ids` pins the ID emitted for each tool call index, so replay never changes an ID the client saw on an earlier chunk. The gap is the chunk where a tool call's ID first appears. With the default `tool_call_id_type` (`random`), `make_tool_call_id` returns `chatcmpl-tool-{random_uuid()}`. If the client retries that chunk with the same `stream_state` (lost response, timeout, retry on another replica), the retry gets a new ID. If the first response reached anyone anyway, the same call now has two IDs. Rerunning a whole stream over the same generate output gives new IDs too. `kimi_k2` IDs (`functions.{name}:{idx}`) are derived from the input, so they aren't affected.

Options:

- **The cache remembers the IDs it assigned** per `(request_id, choice_index, tool call index)`. This only helps on a hit, on the same replica and within the TTL.
- **Derive the ID from the request**, e.g. a hash of `request_id`, `choice_index` and the tool call index. It's stateless, so it works on any replica and could also cover the batch path. But `request_id` is client supplied, so two requests that reuse one would share tool call IDs and it changes what `random` means for `tool_call_id_type`.
- **Document it as a limitation.** A client that retries a chunk treats the retried response as replacing the first one.

#### Done when

- [ ] Parser cache design agreed here (hit check, bounds, concurrency, routing, default)
- [ ] Decision on tool call ID stability for retried calls
- [ ] Cache implemented with tests showing identical output with the cache on and off over the chunked path (plain, reasoning, tool, reasoning + tool, a multi-token chunk, a finish only chunk), including forced evictions midstream
- [ ] Benchmarked on @shimib's setup with and without the cache
- [ ] "Streaming cost" in `derenderer.md` updated

### Alternatives

- **Serialize parser state into `stream_state`.** Dropped. Parsers hold internals we can't cheaply round trip (`prev_tool_call_arr`, `current_tool_id`, `streamed_args_for_tool`, engine lexer buffers) and #32713 was closed as not planned.
- **Parse on the decode pool (#56851).** This is the answer for latency sensitive P/D. It doesn't help consumers that want a stateless render tier or do their own postprocessing.
- **Keep replay only.** Size `renderer_num_workers` for concurrent parsed streams and accept the cost. That's where things are after #50550.
- **Bidirectional streaming derender.** Suggested by @andylolu2. One stream per request holds the parser, so there's no cache, hit check, TTL or routing affinity. It needs a new streaming endpoint (WebSocket or gRPC) and a client change, so it doesn't replace the cache for existing clients. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57571#issuecomment-5764095680 for more details.

### Additional context

- RFC #47161, "Parser state: replay (no opaque serialization)"
- PR #50550 review threads from @sagearc:
  - shared `ChatStreamProcessor`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913908193
  - retaining parser state per stream: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913925664
  - tool call ID stability on retries: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913963783
- Replay benchmark: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56851#issuecomment-5685698033
- Shared per choice `ChatStreamProcessor` for chat serving and derender: #57572
- Batch derender discards the parser's tool call ID: tracked under #42729
- #32713 (unified parser / serializable parser state, closed as not planned)

cc @sagearc @chaunceyjiang @shimib @bbrowning

title: [Bug]: Structured outputs + pipeline parallelism on the V1 model runner: xgrammar FSM desync ("Failed to advance FSM")
body:
### Your current environment

env is not needed

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Used model : qwen 3.5 27b

PP (pipeline_parallel_size > 1) and structured outputs
(xgrammar), requests intermittently fail with a 500. 



```
backend_xgrammar.py: Failed to advance FSM for request <id> for tokens 4754
scheduler.py: Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [4754]. Terminating request.
```

The failure is most reliable right after server start; once the engine is warm
it becomes intermittent.

This only happens when the engine uses the V1 model runner. Models that run on
the V2 model runner are not affected.



## Environment

- vLLM 0.22.1rc1.dev266+g469f3dcf1; code paths below are unchanged on current
  main (c66b19800).
- Model: cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-27B-AWQ-4bit (hybrid / Mamba-style, Qwen3.5).
- 3x A100-40GB.
- Flags: 
```--pipeline-parallel-size 3 --enable-prefix-caching
  --structured-outputs '{"backend":"xgrammar","disable_any_whitespace":true}'
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --attention-backend FLASHINFER
```
-Async scheduling enabled (default, and forced-on by PP).


The model is hybrid with mamba_cache_mode="align" (set automatically when prefix
caching is on), which is listed as unsupported by the V2 model runner
(config/vllm.py: _get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features), so the engine falls
back to the V1 model runner. That fallback is what exposes the bug.


## how to reproduce the bug

Send multiple concurrent chat-completion requests with json schema, right after the server becomes ready
A single request is enough on a cold engine.

100% failure on the first burst, then intermittent.


--------

- PP=3, V1 runner, structured: fails (FSM reject, 500). Reliable on first burst.
- TP=2, V1 runner, structured: **no failures** (105 requests).
- TP=3: cannot start for this model (16 attention heads not divisible by 3),
  which is why PP is used to span 3 GPUs in the first place.
- Plain (non-structured) generation under PP=3: no failures.

title: [RFC]: StructuredOutputManager x Speculative Decoding Refactor
body:
### Motivation.

Simplify the contract between `Scheduler`, grammar backend, and `StructuredOutputManager`, especially when speculative decoding is used.

`StructuredOutputManager` exists because constrained decoding often doesn't kick in until a model has finished reasoning. With speculative decoding, grammar-invalid draft tokens need to be rejected, draft tokens need to temporarily advance grammar state to generate bitmasks, rejected draft tokens should not advance grammar state. Reasoning end boundary can also fall in the middle of the draft token window, so only draft tokens after said boundary should advance grammar state.

`Scheduler` and the `StructuredOutputManager` need to do a careful dance to make this is all correct. This leads to some bugs such as [#34650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34650) -- only recently fixed thanks to [#44297](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44297).

```
Per request inside a scheduler step
1. StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)                         # Should we constrain some draft tokens?
   Grammar.validate_tokens(draft tokens)                                   # Reject grammar invalid draft tokens
2. StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask(...)                            # Generate bitmasks for the draft tokens
3. Verifier runs
4. StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)                         # Should we constrain some draft token? 
   StructuredOutputManager.trim_reasoning_for_advance(verified tokens)     # Trim the draft tokens that are not constrained
   Grammar.accept_tokens(verified tokens)                                  # Advance grammar state
```

In fact, speculative decoding x constrained decoding remains fragile / subtly incorrect:
1. ~~`StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)` treats STRUCTURAL_TAG vs other constraint types differently. It defers non STRUCTURAL_TAG constraints. [#44297](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44297) only fix the strict tool calling case (which uses STRUCTURAL_TAG); [#34650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34650) is still unfixed for JSON, REGEX, and other constraint types.~~ Fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44993
2. ~~`StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)` also doesn't answer "should we constrain some draft tokens?" reliably. It incorrectly infers the draft token window from `num_output_placeholders`.~~ Fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44993
3. `Grammar.validate_tokens(draft_tokens)` only works on a best effort basis -- it doesn't validate any draft token unless all draft tokens should be constrained. We rely on `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask(...)` and rejection sampling to discard grammer-invalid tokens.

### Proposed Change.

Let `StructuredOutputManager` handle the token validation and grammar advancement.

Remove:
- `StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)`
- `StructuredOutputManager.trim_reasoning_for_advance(verified tokens)`

Add:
- `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens(draft tokens)`
- `StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens(verified tokens)`

```
Per request inside a scheduler step
1. StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens(draft tokens)
2. StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask(...)
3. Verifier runs
4. StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens(verified tokens)
```

Internally, `validate_tokens()`, `grammar_bitmask()`, and `accept_tokens()` all use the same `_get_constraint_start()` helper to determine whether and where draft tokens should be constrained and grammar state advanced.

Concretly, `_get_constraint_start()` computes the first token that should be grammar-constrained.

- `validate_tokens()` preserves any unconstrained prefix and validates only the constrained suffix.
- `grammar_bitmask()` emits unconstrained bitmaks before the boundary and constrained bitmasks after it.
- `accept_tokens()` advances the grammar state only on the constrained suffix only

This gives a simpler mental model for the system. The scheduler is responsible for request lifecycle and token plumbing. `StructuredOutputManager` is responsible for draft token validation, bitmask generation, and grammar backends.

~100 insertions, ~200 deletions of changes excluding test updates.

~~Would fix issues like: #34650 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43388~~

### CC List.

@njhill @mgoin @chaunceyjiang @benchislett @arpera 

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [SM120] Field report: running DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash end-to-end on 8x RTX PRO 6000 — pitfall map + working configuration (1M context verified)
body:
## Summary

Cross-posting field data from a 3-day bring-up of **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (769B total, MXFP4 experts, Engram memory) on **8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, consumer Blackwell)**, since SM120 users currently have to rediscover all of this from scratch. Related: #54929 (Triton sparse-MLA fallback — we left perf data there), #5135-tracked flashinfer instantiation gaps.

## What works (final configuration)

- vLLM `deepseekv41-flash-0909` image, TP=8, `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41`
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`
- 1M context enabled: 950K-token double-needle retrieval **correct**, 4584 tok/s prefill throughput (pure-torch logits path, eager mode)
- VRAM: ~91GB/96GB per GPU (Engram tables dominate: 2 x ~100GB shards = 189GiB across the TP group)

## Pitfall map (in the order we hit them)

1. **DeepGEMM autotune hang on first long-context batch** — warmup deadlocks at 128K+; needs skip or eager for first bring-up.
2. **flashinfer sparse-MLA SM120 instantiation gaps** — several `(num_heads, topk)` combos (e.g. `(16, 512)`) missing from `_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH` / prefill dispatch (same family as flashinfer#3828). Vision path hits this too → we ran `--limit-mm-per-prompt {"image":0}` until resolved.
3. **FP8 KV-cache scale layout semantics** — the killer. Block layout is `[64tok x 128B fp8 | 64tok x 4B fp32 scale]` (block-appended), NOT per-token interleaved. Wrong interpretation passes short-prompt smoke tests and **only fails at ≥100K needle retrieval** — silent numerical corruption. Test with long needles, not perplexity.
4. **CUDA graph capture crash with flashinfer ops in graph** (>4K tokens) — resolved for us by replacing the ops with pure-torch; graphs now capture cleanly.
5. **MXFP4 expert path falls back to Marlin** on SM120 (known #30135) — works, perf hit acceptable.

## Verification methodology (cheap, catches #3)

Synthetic doc ~1M tokens with two inserted facts at 50% and 80% depth (e.g. meeting-room password + project codename/lead). Single prompt asking both. Catches numerical corruption that short-prompt tests miss. We publish numbers at 190K and 950K this way.

## Ask

- Would maintainers accept a PR adding the **pure-torch paged-MQA-logits fallback** (auto-selected on SM12x when flashinstantiation is missing)? It's ~90 lines, numerically exact, and would have saved us days. Can also serve as golden reference for #54929's Triton kernels.
- Long-needle (≥100K) test cases for SM12x CI would have caught pitfall 3 upstream.

Env: vLLM 0.1.dev20904 (deepseekv41-flash-0909), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, 8x RTX PRO 6000 96GB.

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash long-decode degeneration after accumulated reasoning decode
body:
### Your current environment

Hardware: 1x NVIDIA B300, ~267 GiB visible VRAM
Runtime: vLLM OpenAI-compatible server
vLLM: 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b
FlashInfer: 0.6.18
Transformers: 5.16.1
Torch: 2.13.0+cu130
CUDA: 13.0

Model: private W4A16 quantized GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint
TP: 1
Context length: ~372k

Reasoning parser: glm45
Tool-call parser: glm47
Native tools enabled

reasoning_effort=max
clear_thinking=true

MTP/EAGLE: disabled for the tests below
Prefix cache: tested on and off; issue happens in both cases

Workload: private long-running multi-agent / sub-agent coding workload with native tool calls.
I cannot post raw prompts or tool outputs publicly.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Purpose

I am running GLM-5.3-Flash in a long-running multi-agent / sub-agent coding workload with native tools and `reasoning_effort=max`.

The model works well for many turns, then after a long session it can suddenly collapse inside `reasoning`.

### Bug

The collapse is repetitive low-entropy output such as:

```text
= = = = = = = = ...
```

or:

```text
.0.0.0.0.0.0.0.0...
```

I logged raw SSE before the stream reaches the client. The bad output is already present in raw vLLM SSE, for example many deltas like:

```json
{"delta":{"reasoning":" ="}}
```

So this does not look like a client-side stream reconstruction issue.

When it happens, no tool call is emitted. The model stays stuck in `reasoning`.

### Already checked

- MTP on/off: issue happens in both cases.
- Prefix cache on/off: issue happens in both cases.
- Sampling/repetition settings: issue still happens.
- H200 and B300: similar issue, so not B300-only.
- SGLang: similar degeneration after 15-20 min.
- Lower reasoning or aggressive windowing can delay it, but they are not acceptable fixes for this workload.

Also tested/backported:

- Normalize assistant `content:null` + `tool_calls` to `content:""` before chat templating.
- PR #56635 / commit `b150783`.

The issue still happens.

### Reasoning replay

The client was originally replaying old assistant reasoning into later tool turns. I added a proxy that removes old `reasoning_content`, `reasoning`, and `thinking` before forwarding to vLLM.

In one failing session, the proxy removed ~471k chars of old reasoning and the forwarded request had zero historical `reasoning_content`.

This helped a lot, but the late-session collapse still came back.

### Replay tests

I replayed captured forwarded requests directly against vLLM, without the client.

1. Cold replay of the exact failing request: healthy, ended with `finish_reason=tool_calls`.

2. Five parallel cold replays of the same request: all healthy, all ended with `finish_reason=tool_calls`.

3. Sequential replay of historical requests: after 76 successful requests, request 77 collapsed into `.1.1.1...` then `.0.0.0...`.

4. Cold replay of request 77 only: healthy.

5. Prefill-only warmup: replayed the first 76 historical requests with `max_tokens=1`, then request 77 unchanged. Result: request 77 was healthy.

Key difference:

| Test | Prior prompt tokens | Prior decode/reasoning tokens | request 77 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Cold request 77 | 0 | 0 | healthy |
| 76 prefill-only requests, then request 77 | ~2.76M | ~76 | healthy |
| 76 full requests, then request 77 | ~2.76M | ~200k | collapsed |

So it looks more related to accumulated decode/reasoning than to prefill volume alone.

### Question

Could this be a correctness issue in the GLM-5.3 `glm5next` decode path, for example KDA/recurrent state lifecycle, slot reuse, hybrid KV/KDA mapping, CUDA graph replay, or numerical drift during long decode?

Is there a recommended branch or patch set for GLM-5.3-Flash long agentic workloads on single-GPU Blackwell/B300?

### Privacy

The workload is private and proprietary, so I cannot post raw prompts, raw tool outputs, or raw `forwarded.json` publicly.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Long multi-turn agentic sessions on GLM-5.3-Flash (FP8) intermittently collapse into repeated tokens / shell-fragment word salad ((tmp)(tmp)…). Same config: clean on 0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187(08-26), degenerates on 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b (09-08); **Version delta:** | Component | GOOD `sha256:2c6da6c6…` (clean) | BAD `sha256:819ec9c0…` (degenerates) | |---|---|---| | vLLM | `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187` | `0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b` | | flashinfer-python | 0.6.17 | **0.6.18** | | transformers | 5.15.1 | **5.16.1** | | torch | 2.13.0+cu130 | 2.13.0+cu130 | | CUDA runtime | 13.0.88 | 13.0.88 | So the regression lives in one (or more) of: the vLLM commit range `g487ecf187…g385dce36b`, **FlashInfer 0.6.17→0.6.18** (attention kernels — directly on the hybrid path), or **transformers 5.15.1→5.16.1** (tokenizer/chat-template/generation). torch and CUDA are unchanged. ## Symptom - Coherent, then degenerates into repeated/incoherent tokens after many tool-call turns / large context. - Silent: HTTP 200, normal `finished_reason`, no errors, no preemptions. - Single-turn and short requests always clean. ## Minimal reproduction attempt (could NOT reproduce synthetically) Against the bad build, all of the following returned **coherent** output (~30+ requests total, `clear_thinking` on and off): - Single-turn coding / classification prompts — clean. - 8-way concurrent short requests — clean. - 10-turn tool-call history (`bash` tool, half the assistant turns tool_use-only/no text, shell-style tool_results incl. `/tmp`), then a final summary turn — clean. - ~34k-token context, `max_tokens` up to 3000, `reasoning_effort=max`, run twice (2nd pass = guaranteed prefix-cache hits) — clean. → **Only reproduces in real agentic clients (Claude Code / OpenCode-style) over long sessions.** Not triggered by any isolated request I could construct. title: [Bug]: Qwen3 parser turns tool-call markup the model quotes into real tool calls (names outside request.tools, and duplicates of offered ones)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `v0.28.0` (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0`), xgrammar 0.2.3
- Qwen3.8-27B, NVFP4 checkpoint; chat template sha256 `0a20a4673d45476ed88dcb4a60b6af35ca202ae470fee6fd2bd419758aabd9ab`
- `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'` (reproduced with and without speculation)
- RTX 5090 (sm_120), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130
- `/v1/chat/completions`, streaming and non-streaming

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When the model writes tool-call markup as *text* — quoting the format in its
reasoning, showing the caller an example, echoing the template's own
placeholder block — the `ParserEngine` transitions in `vllm/parser/qwen3.py`
(`(REASONING, TOOL_START)`, `(TOOL_BETWEEN, FUNC_PREFIX)`) fire on it, and the
response carries tool calls the model did not make. Two distinct classes:

1. **Names that are not in `request.tools`** — `function_name`, `...`,
   straight from the chat template's example block.
2. **Duplicates of an offered name** — the model shows a `get_weather` block
   and then makes the real call; the client receives two or three.

Both reach the client as ordinary `tool_calls`, so a harness executes them.

#### Minimal reproduction (parser-level, no server)

```python
from vllm.parser.qwen3 import Qwen3Parser
# tools = [get_weather(city: string)], thinking on
text = ("The format is:\n<tool_call>\n<function=function_name>\n<parameter=parameter_name>\nvalue\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>\nNow call it.\n</think>\n\n"
        "<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>\n<parameter=city>\nParis\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>")
# extract_tool_calls(text) ->
#   [('function_name', '{"parameter_name": "value"}'), ('get_weather', '{"city": "Paris"}')]
# streaming path: identical two calls
```

#### Measured on a live server

8 cases x thinking off/on x sync/stream, 100 repeats per cell, concurrency 4,
model-default sampling (T 1.0 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 20), 3,200 requests per
arm, every failure carrying its raw generation. In ordinary cases the defect
is rare — 1-2 out-of-set phantoms per 1,600 thinking-on requests, the same
with speculative decoding on or off (it is the parser, not the drafter).

One prompt makes it the common case: *ask the model to show the tool-call
block it is about to use, then use it.* 100 repeats per cell:

| | unpatched 0.28.0 | with `validate_tool_names=True` (i.e. #50986) |
|---|---|---|
| out-of-set names (`function_name`, `...`) | **8** | **0** |
| duplicates of an offered name | 168 | 168 |
| legitimate calls withheld | — | **0** |
| pass, 800 requests | 393/800 | 421/800 |

Thinking on, 76-84 of every 100 responses to that prompt carry a duplicated
in-set call, in both arms.

### The fix for class 1 is already open: #50986

`ParserEngineConfig.validate_tool_names`
(`vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine_config.py:104`) gates `_emit_name_delta`,
`_handle_tool_end` and `extract_tool_calls` (`parser_engine.py:798, 858,
1033`), so a call whose name is not in `request.tools` is never emitted on
either path. `glm47_moe.py:179` opts in; `qwen3_config` does not. #50986
sets it. Measured on a deployed server, that PR:

- removes the out-of-set class outright (8 -> 0 above);
- **withholds nothing legitimate** — every `no_call` under the patch is a
  generation that emitted only placeholder markup; not one raw contained
  `<function=get_weather>`;
- leaves the #39056 implicit-end path (an offered call inside `<think>` with
  no `</think>`) parsing exactly as before — verified at parser level, sync
  and streaming.

### Class 2 is not covered by #50986, and only partly by #57553

Of 336 duplicate-call failures with raw generations kept:

- **86** contain a ``` fence — the shape [#57553](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57553) / #57541 addresses;
- **93** have a `<tool_call>` before `</think>`, i.e. quoted inside reasoning;
- the rest are unfenced quotations in ordinary content.

So fenced-example handling catches about a quarter of what we see. The
general case — the model showing the markup and then using it — needs the
parser to distinguish a quotation from an emission. Filing this so the two
classes are on the record separately; happy to supply raw generations for
either (fixtures are synthetic weather/file calls, nothing private).

Related: #39056 (opposite direction — calls inside `<think>` must not be
lost), #57541 / #57553 (fenced examples), #58105 (streaming loses calls when
the grammar admits ordinary-token delimiters), #54808 (`tool_choice`
`required`/named not enforced on chat completions for the XML parsers — a
grammar would have refused the out-of-set names).

AI assistance was used to investigate the code paths, build the measurement harness and draft this report; the human submitter reviewed it and ran everything described above on his own hardware.

The model generates a valid prefix, then enters a degenerate loop repeating a phrase with minor variations indefinitely until `max_tokens` is hit. **Observations:** - Occurs with both BF16 and quantized (FP8, NVFP4) weights - Much higher frequency when grammar/JSON schema constraints are applied via xgrammar - Not specific to tensor parallelism configuration - Occurs on both vLLM v0.19.x and latest main - **Not a vLLM-specific issue** — the same behavior has been reported across multiple deployment platforms (see related issues below) ### Related issues (cross-platform) This appears to be a model-level issue affecting all serving platforms, not specific to vLLM: - **google-deepmind/gemma#622** — Gemma 4 repetition issue (general) - **google-deepmind/gemma#610** — Cloudflare Gemma-4-26B-A4B repetition - **google/gemma-4-31B-it HF discussion#63** — Repetition reported on Google Vertex AI official deployment - **vllm#39130** — Related: `--reasoning-parser gemma4` silently disables structured output when `enable_thinking=false` ### Analysis The repetition pattern seems to be a model-level tendency that is amplified by grammar-constrained decoding. When xgrammar restricts the token space to valid JSON tokens, the model's slight repetition bias becomes a strong loop because the grammar prevents the model from generating an EOS or breaking out of the pattern. Possible mitigations at the vLLM level: - `repetition_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` sampling parameters partially help but do not fully prevent the issue - The interaction between xgrammar bitmask and Gemma 4's attention pattern may deserve investigation ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions. ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Reproduction ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="x") response = client.chat.completions.create( model="google/gemma-4-31B-it", messages=[ {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the patient's symptoms in a structured format."} ], response_format={ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": { "name": "diagnosis", "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "patient_information": {"type": "string"}, "diagnosis_and_complaints": {"type": "string"}, }, "required": ["patient_information", "diagnosis_and_complaints"] } } }, max_tokens=2000, ) print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Docs] Document NIXL KV connector metrics aggregation semantics
body:
## Summary

The NIXL KV connector logs transfer metrics periodically:

```
KV Transfer metrics: Num successful transfers=4, Avg xfer time (ms)=1.381, P90 xfer time (ms)=2.601, Avg post time (ms)=0.672, P90 post time (ms)=0.801, Avg MB per transfer=2.25, Throughput (MB/s)=1629.549, Avg number of descriptors=72.0
```

Currently there is no documentation explaining what these metrics represent, especially in the context of **multi-rank (TP > 1) deployments**. This has already caused confusion among users.

## Current behavior

All metrics are **aggregated across all TP ranks** before summary stats are computed:

1. Each TP rank independently records per-transfer telemetry (`transfer_duration`, `post_duration`, `bytes_transferred`, `num_descriptors`) via `NixlKVConnectorStats.record_transfer()` in [`stats.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/stats.py).
2. Stats from all ranks are concatenated via `aggregate()` (`list.extend()`).
3. `reduce()` computes averages, percentiles, and throughput over the **combined** pool of observations from all ranks.

This means:
- **"Num successful transfers"** is the total count across all ranks, not per-rank.
- **"Avg MB per transfer"** is the average over all individual rank-level transfers, not the total bytes moved for a single KV cache transfer operation.
- **"Throughput (MB/s)"** is `total_MB_all_ranks / total_time_all_ranks` — effectively an average per-rank throughput, not the aggregate system throughput.
- **Percentiles (P90)** are computed over the combined distribution of all ranks' transfer times.

This is unintuitive because users may expect metrics to reflect per-engine totals or aggregate system throughput.

## What needs to be documented

1. **Docstrings in `stats.py`**: Add clear documentation to `NixlKVConnectorStats` explaining that stats are aggregated across all TP ranks and what each metric represents in that context.
2. **Inline comments in `reduce()`**: Clarify the semantics of throughput and averages — that they are per-rank averages over the combined observation pool.
3. **Docstrings in `metrics.py`**: Document the `observe()` → `aggregate()` → `reduce()` → `log()` pipeline and the fact that stats arrive pre-aggregated across workers.
4. **(Optional) Docs page**: Add a section to the disaggregated serving documentation explaining how to interpret the KV Transfer metrics log line.

## Relevant files

- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/stats.py` — `NixlKVConnectorStats` (recording, aggregation, reduction)
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/metrics.py` — `KVConnectorLogging` (observe/log pipeline), `KVConnectorStats` (base class)

## Context

See related discussion: metrics are aggregated across ranks rather than reported per-rank or per-engine. This is a deliberate design choice (fire-and-forget from workers), but it needs to be clearly documented so users can correctly interpret the numbers.

title: [RFC]: Efficient Routed-Expert Replay with Prefix Omission and KV Cache Offloading
body:
### Motivation.

vLLM can return routed-expert IDs for replay and training. In multi-turn workloads, however, returning routes for the full prompt on every request repeatedly gathers, transfers, and concatenates historical data that the caller already owns.

Prefix caching avoids recomputing KV, but the routed-expert output path does not currently share the same ownership boundary. KV offloading makes this harder because a cached block may be restored to a different GPU block while the routed-expert table is indexed by GPU slots.

This RFC proposes prefix omission for routed-expert output and defines the compatibility contract for same-engine KV offloading, while preserving the existing behavior by default.

**Preliminary performance.** Step 3.5 FP8 on 8 × H200 (TP=8, PP=1), with async scheduling enabled and KV offloading disabled: 128 concurrent lanes × 100 turns, starting with 640 prompt tokens and adding 320 generated + 320 random tokens per turn, with a 1 s inter-turn pause. RPM includes these pauses; results are normalized to routed-expert return disabled. 

| Configuration | Mean latency (s) | RPM |
|-|-|-|
| Routed-expert return disabled | 5.695 (1.00×) | 1144.20 (1.00×) |
| Full routed-expert output | 6.642 (1.17×) | 999.29 (0.87×) |
| Prefix omission | 5.793 (1.02×) | 1127.64 (0.99×) |

### Proposed Change.

## Current behavior

Workers return routed-expert IDs with model output. `RoutedExpertsManager` stores them by full-attention GPU slot, gathers prompt routes with NumPy indexing, and appends decode routes to request state. The API returns the complete accumulated route sequence. Routed-expert return is currently rejected when KV transfer is enabled.

## Scope and non-goals

This RFC covers routed-expert prefix omission and compatibility with same-engine store/load KV offloading. Initial connector support targets SimpleCPUOffloadConnector, OffloadingConnector, and MooncakeStoreConnector. OffloadingConnector support is initially limited to the built-in CPUOffloadingSpec; TieringOffloadingSpec, secondary storage tiers, and custom offloading specs are out of scope. Prefill-decode disaggregation, `PP`/`DCP`/`PCP` greater than 1, more than two overlapping asynchronous scheduler batches, and the caller-side route storage implementation are out of scope for the initial implementation.

## Proposed API

Add `--enable-omit-prefix-routed-experts`. It is valid only with `--enable-return-routed-experts` and is disabled by default.

When prefix omission is enabled, vLLM omits routed experts for the cached prefix. The caller is responsible for receiving and retaining returned route chunks and correctly merging them with previously retained routes under the same session/cache identity. vLLM does not manage or verify this cross-request accumulation. 

The first completed GPU-plus-connector cache lookup sets `request.num_cached_tokens` as the immutable cached-prefix boundary. Scheduling, preemption, reset, and KV load may change computed or resident KV state, but must not change this boundary.

The returned range starts at:

```python
prompt_start = max(
    request.sampling_params.routed_experts_prompt_start or 0,
    request.num_cached_tokens,
)
```

## Internal design

**Prefix omission.** Slice the prompt slot mapping at `prompt_start` before the NumPy gather. This avoids materializing routed-expert data that will be discarded and leaves decode handling unchanged.

**Session isolation.** Use the existing request `cache_salt` mechanism to encode the stable session/cache identity in the first block hash, so shared prefixes, such as system prompts, are not reused across identities whose routed experts are owned separately. All three initial connector targets already preserve cache salt through their existing block-hash keys.

**Recovery after preemption.** The initial cache lookup remains unchanged and may combine GPU and connector hits. Once decode has started, routes for previously forwarded output tokens are retained in the frontend state of the same request, so recovery may use normal GPU and connector lookup. Before decode starts, recovery caps GPU prefix reuse at `request.num_cached_tokens` and bypasses external lookup. We will add a lightweight bypass hook to each of the three initial connector targets, preserving the initialization, state updates, and cleanup required for a zero-external-hit scheduling path without initiating a new external lookup or load plan.

**Offload safety (optional).** This proposal supports same-engine store/load offloading, not prefill-decode disaggregation. As an optional defense in depth, the scheduler may derive the routed-expert slots for the accepted external-token range from the allocated request block table. The scheduler invalidates these slots before the external KV load begins and reapplies invalidation after storing an older asynchronous output, without clearing slots for newly computed tokens outside that range. No routed-expert sidecar is transferred with KV.

## Alternatives considered

- **Always return the full route history.** This preserves current semantics but retains repeated collection and transfer overhead.
- **Transfer routed experts as a KV sidecar.** This restores historical routes with offloaded KV but substantially expands the connector protocol and data volume.

## Compatibility

- With prefix omission disabled, routed-expert output is unchanged.
- With routed-expert return enabled, KV offloading is supported only when prefix omission is enabled and the connector provides the external-lookup bypass capability. Both requirements are checked during server initialization; unsupported configurations are rejected, and every child of a composite connector must support the bypass capability.

## Risks

- **Cache identity consistency.** The three initial connector targets preserve the GPU cache identity, including `cache_salt`. This has not been established for other connectors; losing the salt during external key construction may allow cross-session hits and cause vLLM to omit routes the caller does not own. Requests without a stable session/cache identity are rejected rather than falling back to full routed-expert output.
- **Caller-side route reconstruction.** The caller must retain and correctly merge routes across requests sharing the same identity. Tokenization is not associative across independently rendered fragments, so route reconstruction must preserve alignment between expert positions and the corresponding tokens. vLLM does not verify the caller's retained routes or cross-request reconstruction.

### Feedback Period.

Two weeks.

### CC List.

_No response_

### Any Other Things.

Frontend concatenation of routed-expert chunks can block an API process when many requests finish together. Existing deployments can reduce this contention by increasing `--api-server-count`; this is operational guidance, not part of the proposed design.

A preliminary implementation is available in [this branch](https://github.com/cccyy123/vllm/tree/routed-expert-prefix-omit) for reference. Optional slot invalidation is not included.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Feature]: Migration plan for ROCm 7.14 / TheRock production release (containers + wheels)
body:
# [Feature]: Migration plan for ROCm 7.14 / TheRock production release (containers + wheels)

## 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

AMD released **ROCm 7.14** on 2026-07-15 — the **first production release built on TheRock**, AMD's new open-source build and release system. The 7.9–7.13 preview train is complete, and AMD's release notes explicitly encourage users on the legacy packaging line (7.2.x and older) to migrate:

- Release blog: https://rocm.blogs.amd.com/ecosystems-and-partners/rocm-7.14-blog/README.html
- TheRock: https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock
- Release notes: https://rocm.docs.amd.com/en/docs-7.14.0/about/release-notes.html
- Transition guide: https://rocm.docs.amd.com/en/docs-7.14.0/about/transition-guide-TheRock.html

### Current state in vLLM upstream

vLLM's ROCm support is currently straddling both packaging worlds:

- **Container path (legacy):** `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` on `main` pins `BASE_IMAGE=rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete`, i.e. the legacy (non-TheRock) packaging line, with PyTorch built from the ROCm fork `release/2.11` branch and pinned Triton / flash-attention / AITER (`v0.1.16.post3`) / MORI (`v1.1.0`) builds on top.
- **Wheel path (already TheRock):** the ROCm vLLM wheels at `wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/` pull in TheRock-published `rocm-sdk-core` / `rocm-sdk-libraries-gfx<target>` wheels as transitive dependencies.

Now that TheRock is the production line, it would help downstream consumers (distributions, enterprise inference stacks, CI systems that build vLLM from source) to have a public plan for converging on it.

### What this issue is asking for

Not an immediate version bump — rather, a tracking issue / statement of direction from maintainers and the AMD upstream team on:

1. **Base image:** Is a TheRock-based equivalent of `rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:*-complete` planned/available for `Dockerfile.rocm_base`? TheRock introduces a different packaging model (ROCm Core SDK + optional expansion SDKs, runfile installer, pip wheels) rather than the monolithic `-complete` apt install, so this is likely not a one-line change.
2. **PyTorch pairing:** ROCm 7.14 validates against PyTorch 2.12 (which also switches the PyTorch Profiler to rocprofiler-SDK as its ROCm backend). What's the plan for moving the `Dockerfile.rocm_base` PyTorch build from the ROCm fork `release/2.11` branch, and does the ROCm/pytorch fork build cleanly against TheRock layouts?
3. **Dependency pins:** Do the current Triton, flash-attention, AITER, and MORI pins build and pass against 7.14/TheRock, or do they need coordinated bumps?
4. **Convergence with the wheel path:** Should the container build move toward the same `rocm-sdk-*` wheel approach the pip path already uses (which would unify the two install stories), or stay on OS packages?
5. **Timeline:** Which vLLM release is targeted to be the first validated against ROCm 7.14, for both `main` and the release Docker images (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm`)? Note that vLLM upstream is already at v0.25.1 as of this writing, two minor releases ahead of the v0.23.0 that ROCm 7.14 packages, so there's already a version gap to close on top of the ROCm-version gap.
6. **GPU coverage:** Any expected changes to the supported `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH` set (currently gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950;gfx1100;gfx1101;gfx1200;gfx1201;gfx1150;gfx1151) when moving to TheRock builds?

### Why now

- AMD's 7.14 release notes ship vLLM 0.23.0 packaged as deployment-ready inside the ROCm distribution, so the AMD-side integration clearly exists; upstream visibility on the convergence plan would help everyone else align.
- Downstream consumers (Linux distributions, enterprise inference products, wheel-building pipelines) need lead time to plan their own migrations off the legacy 7.2.x line, and the vLLM base image pin is the anchor for that planning.
- TheRock's fully open, pure-CMake build and public CI are a good fit for vLLM's recent push to make ROCm a first-class, continuously validated platform.

## Alternatives

- Keep the container path on the legacy 7.2.x line until it reaches EOL and only then migrate — but this delays the benefits of TheRock's nightly releases and public CI, and leaves the container and wheel paths on divergent ROCm packaging indefinitely.
- Track this in ROCm/TheRock instead (there is an `ecosystem: vLLM` label there) — happy to move/cross-link if maintainers prefer that as the canonical location.

## Additional context

Related: TheRock issues labeled `ecosystem: vLLM`: https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/labels/ecosystem%3A%20vLLM

cc AMD upstream maintainers (feel free to tag the folks driving the ROCm first-class-platform work).

### The bug For Mistral models served with `--tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice`, every chat completion request — including plain-text ones with `tool_choice="none"` and no `tools`— triggers a full rebuild of `MistralToolParser` → `ParserEngine` → `StreamingParserEngine`, which compiles `regex` patterns over the tokenizer's entire special-token vocabulary (`_build_drop_info` in `vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py`). This runs **synchronously on the main asyncio event loop**, not inside the renderer's `ThreadPoolExecutor` (unlike tokenization itself, which is offloaded via `make_async`). Under concurrent load this becomes a hard admission bottleneck: the event loop can't advance anything else while blocked on it, so requests back up long before ever reaching the scheduler. Model: `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603`, served with `--tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mistral --tensor-parallel-size 2` on 2×H200. Confirmed present, unchanged, in both v0.29.0 and v0.30.0 (checked directly against source). Root cause is `online_renderer.py`'s `preprocess_chat`: ```python is_mistral_grammar_eligible = ( tool_parser is not None and is_mistral_tool_parser(tool_parser) and is_mistral_tokenizer(tokenizer) and tokenizer.supports_grammar ) should_adjust_request = ( parser.reasoning_parser_cls is not None or tool_choice != "none" or is_mistral_grammar_eligible # forces adjust_request unconditionally for Mistral ) ``` The comment above it explains this is intentional ("so that the grammar factory can prevent special-token leakage"), but the expensive part (`_build_drop_info`) depends only on the fixed tokenizer vocabulary/parser config — not on per-request `tools` or content — so it looks memoizable rather than needing reconstruction on every request. **Reproduction:** 1. Serve a Mistral model: `vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603 --tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mistral --tensor-parallel-size 2 ...` 2. Send concurrent `tool_choice="none"` requests (no `tools`), e.g. `vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 200 --request-rate 16`. 3. Observe TTFT balloon and engine `Running` (from the periodic `Engine 000: ...` log line) stay near-flat despite high offered load, while GPU/KV-cache usage stays near-idle. 4. Remove `--tool-call-parser`/`--enable-auto-tool-choice`/`--reasoning-parser` and rerun — throughput and TTFT return to normal. **Results observed vs. expected**, same benchmark (200 requests, request-rate=16, random 512-token prompts): | | With the three flags | Without (diagnostic) | |---|---|---| | Mean TTFT | 39,013 ms | 101 ms | | Output throughput | 604 tok/s | 3,213 tok/s | | Engine `Running` (concurrent) | capped ~3-6 | 45-84 | | GPU KV cache usage | ~0.1% | ~1.8% | Expected: `Running` should scale with offered load regardless of these flags being set, the same way it does without them. Confirmed via `py-spy dump --pid ` mid-load that the `MainThread` (not a worker thread) is caught inside this exact construction path, with locals directly showing `tool_choice: "none"`, `is_mistral_grammar_eligible: True`, `should_adjust_request: True` for a request with no tools: ``` _create_chat_completion (vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py:275) render_chat_request (serving.py:240) render_chat (vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py:192) preprocess_chat (online_renderer.py:718) [tool_choice: "none", is_mistral_grammar_eligible: True, should_adjust_request: True] MistralToolParser.__init__ (vllm/parser/engine/adapters.py:167) MistralParser.__init__ (vllm/parser/mistral.py:279) ParserEngine.__init__ (vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py:107) StreamingParserEngine.__init__ (vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py:133) _build_drop_info (streaming_parser_engine.py:73) regex.compile(...) # compiling patterns over hundreds of special tokens, per request ``` **Suggested fix:** cache `_build_drop_info`'s result (or the constructed `StreamingParserEngine`'s tokenizer-dependent state) keyed on tokenizer identity + parser config, separate from the genuinely per-request-stateful parts of the streaming parser — so `adjust_request` doesn't redo vocabulary-wide regex compilation on every request. - [x] Searched existing issues (closest match found: #57571, which covers a related but distinct cost — output-side streaming derender replay — not this input-side per-request construction) and checked the docs chatbot. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description For a BERT-style cross encoder, `padding="max_length"` pads `input_ids` correctly but assigns every padding token the last real token's `token_type_id`. In a query/document pair that value is normally 1, so padding is incorrectly treated as part of the document segment instead of using the tokenizer's `pad_token_type_id` of 0. BERT consumes token-type embeddings, so accepted `/score` and `/rerank` requests can run on different segment IDs from the tokenizer's intended input. This can change scores, rank order, and threshold decisions. ## Reproduction Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32512913/repro_cross_encoder.py), run: ```bash python repro.py 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The reproducer uses vLLM's released rerank request, tokenization parameters, post-tokenization logic, and worker-side token-type compression. An in-memory BERT tokenizer provides the Transformers reference result, so no model download or GPU is required. The script exits with status 1 when the bug is reproduced. ## Actual result Both paths produce the same padded input IDs: ```text [2, 5, 3, 6, 3, 0, 0, 0] ``` vLLM produces: ```text token_type_ids = [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1] ``` ## Expected result Transformers uses the tokenizer's padding token type: ```text token_type_ids = [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0] ``` Full log is here: [reproducer_cross_encoder.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32512950/reproducer_cross_encoder.log). ## Root cause `_apply_post_tokenization_to_token_type_ids()` pads with `token_type_ids[-1]` instead of `tokenizer.pad_token_type_id`. The following compression step stores only one zero-to-one boundary. That representation can encode `0*1*`, but not the correct right-padded shape `0*1*0*`, so the worker also reconstructs all padded positions as type 1. ## Related PR [PR #47772](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47772) fixes a different boundary problem after truncation. It does not change max-length padding or the single-boundary representation, so this case remains reproducible in vLLM 0.29.0. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Feature][KV cache] Support fine-grained prefix hits for sliding-window groups
body:
## Motivation

Multi-turn agent workloads re-send a large stable prefix every turn, so prefix-cache quality dominates TTFT. We run a Qwen3.5-class hybrid (16 full-attention + 48 linear/GDN layers) with a DFlash2 speculative draft whose 5 layers are all `sliding_attention` (`sliding_window=2048`), and measured reuse capped far below what the fine-grained path would allow — because the sliding-window manager disables fine-grained hits for the shared lookup boundary.

## Precise behavior (source of both `0.26.1rc1.dev926+gb05ae5dc0` and current `main`, verified 2026-08-25)

In a hybrid coordinator using fine-grained align-mode Mamba hits, any coarser cache group whose manager lacks fine-grained lookup disables fine-grained hits for the shared lookup boundary ([`kv_cache_coordinator.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py), the `enable_partial_hash_hits` gating): `SlidingWindowManager` sets `supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup = False` and its block size differs from the hash unit, so `--prefix-match-unit 16` is accepted and then disabled with a single boot warning —

```
WARNING [kv_cache_coordinator.py] Disabling fine-grained prefix-cache hits
because these KV cache managers require block-aligned lookups:
SlidingWindowManager.
```

— a warning-only fallback that is easy to miss. The SWA lookup itself asserts *"Fine-grained partial hits are not supported for sliding window now"*, which reads as an acknowledged TODO.

In our layout the sliding-window group exists **only because of the spec-decode draft**; the target has zero windowed layers, and its full-attention and Mamba managers both support fine-grained lookup.

### Observed effect (our stack; environment below)

Identical immediate replay (same prompt, same `cache_salt`, single-request `/metrics` windows, deterministic across repeats):

| prompt tokens | cached-hit tokens | fraction |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1517 | 0 | 0.00 |
| 2484 | 0 | 0.00 |
| 4187 | 1648 | 0.39 |
| 6130 | 3296 | 0.54 |
| 8285 | 6592 | 0.80 |
| 9766 | 6592 | 0.68 |
| 10228 | 8240 | 0.81 |
| 14572 | 11536 | 0.79 |

Usable replay = `(floor((N-1)/1648) - 1) * 1648` **on this specific configuration** (model, quantization, block-size resolution, sparse-retention default, EAGLE/dflash config — a different quant resolved the mamba-page block bump to 1600 instead of 1648). Real two-turn agent sessions reproduce the law exactly (6/6 reps matching the prediction to 4 decimals). Prefix caching works and helps (TTFT 2.24 s → 0.81 s warm at 9.8k tokens) — it is capped well below what fine-grained hits should allow. We have not tested whether SWA fine-grained support alone lifts the cap under EAGLE: per #52371, FA fine hits + Mamba + EAGLE can still reconcile down a whole physical Mamba block, so Mamba boundary checkpoints (#53614) may also be required.

## Ask

1. Implement fine-grained (partial) prefix hits for sliding-window groups — completing the acknowledged TODO. We're happy to contribute; the design questions below are exactly where we'd want maintainer direction first:
   - mapping fine candidate boundaries to the physical block run covering the window (null padding that preserves physical block-table indices);
   - EAGLE drop semantics when the block list is physical;
   - retention: keeping every physical block needed to reconstruct a registered fine boundary's window.
2. Related: under interleaved-session memory pressure, one evicted tail block invalidates an entire SWA hit (#48435). Fine-grained SWA retention should be designed with that failure mode in mind.

## Alternatives considered

- Disabling speculative decoding removes the windowed draft group and lifts the veto (trade-off: decode throughput).
- A non-windowed draft, if compatible, same effect.
- Accepting the coarse ceiling (current state; documented in our ops notes).
- We looked for a coordinator-level bypass (excluding the draft group from the veto or from lookup) and concluded it is unsound without per-group computed-token boundaries — the coordinator's single shared `num_local_computed_tokens` would claim draft KV that does not exist.

## Reproduction (CPU, manager-level)

GPU-free reproduction of the veto and assertion (source-deterministic): construct a hybrid `kv_cache_config` with FullAttention + SlidingWindow + align-mode Mamba groups, instantiate `KVCacheCoordinator` with `hash_block_size=16`, and observe (a) the "Disabling fine-grained prefix-cache hits … SlidingWindowManager" warning with `enable_partial_hash_hits == False`, and (b) `SlidingWindowManager.find_longest_cache_hit` raising "does not support fine-grained (partial) cache hits" when `alignment_tokens < block_size`. Single-file script (stdlib + vllm import) plus the full calibration/sweep harness and logs available on request or as a follow-up comment. (The serving-level numbers above used a private model stack; environment below.)

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.26.1rc1.dev926+gb05ae5dc0` (nightly wheel); `main` checked 2026-08-25 for the veto + assertion (present).
- Target: Qwen3.5-class hybrid, FP8, 16 full-attention + 48 linear/GDN layers; draft: DFlash2, 5 × `sliding_attention`, window 2048.
- `--enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`; mamba cache mode auto-`align` (boot log); attention block size auto-bumped 16 → 1648 by the mamba page-size rule (boot log).
- GPUs: 2× RTX 5090; driver/CUDA details available (`nvidia-smi` dump on request).

## Related

- #53504 (our earlier report: Mamba retention replay-boundary misses on this hybrid — the sparse-retention side of the same mechanics)
- #53670 (our earlier report: EAGLE last-block drop costing one 1648-token block per hit — the drop side)
- #52371 (pinned mamba align+EAGLE prefix-cache defects — the reconciliation limitation above)
- #53614 + #52959 (Mamba internal checkpoints / partial prefix caching with spec decoding — possible prerequisite substrate)
- #48435 (hybrid-SWA reuse collapse under interleaved-session eviction — adjacent retention/pressure failure, distinct issue)
- #51250, #45238 (hybrid prefix-caching effectiveness reports)

---

*Disclosure: this issue was drafted with AI assistance and reviewed adversarially (Codex CLI); measurements and source citations verified by the author.*

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description `/score` accepts `max_tokens_per_query` and `max_tokens_per_doc`, but the final query or document can still contain more tokens than the requested limit. This happens with ordinary CJK text and emoji ZWJ sequences. The request succeeds with HTTP 200, so this is not an unsupported configuration or a validation error. Callers cannot reliably enforce the documented per-query or per-document token budgets for multilingual input. Extra tokens consume context and compute and can change scores or downstream overlength behavior. ## Reproduction Start the server: ```bash MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \ --served-model-name qwen3-embed \ --runner pooling \ --convert embed \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8036 \ --max-model-len 512 \ --enforce-eager \ 2>&1 | tee server.log ``` In another terminal, use the script [repro_unicode.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32511832/repro_unicode.py): ```bash python repro.py --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" \ 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The script exits with status 1 when the bug is reproduced. ## Actual result | Limited input | Text | Limit | Character slice | Retokenized count | Prompt tokens | Expected upper bound | |---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | document | `中 文 测试` | 3 | `中 文 测` | 4 | 8 | 7 | | document | `😵‍💫x` | 2 | `😵‍` | 3 | 7 | 6 | | document control | `one two three four` | 3 | `one two three` | 3 | 7 | 7 | | query | `中 文 测试` | 3 | `中 文 测` | 4 | 8 | 7 | | query control | `one two three four` | 3 | `one two three` | 3 | 7 | 7 | For the CJK case, the original document has four tokens. After requesting a limit of three, vLLM still reports the same eight prompt tokens as the unlimited request. The same result occurs when that text is the query and the request uses `max_tokens_per_query=3`. Full log is here: [server_unicode.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32511885/server_unicode.log). ## Expected result After `max_tokens_per_doc=N` is applied, the document passed to the model should contain at most `N` content tokens. The same invariant should hold for `max_tokens_per_query`. ## Root cause `truncate_text_to_tokens()` tokenizes the full string, takes the end character offset of token `N`, and returns `text[:char_end]`. The scoring path then tokenizes that character slice again. Token offsets are not guaranteed to form safe retokenization boundaries. Multiple byte-fallback tokens can share or overlap a character span, and BPE merges can change at the new end of the string. The returned substring can therefore tokenize to more than `N` tokens. ## Related issues [#38651](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38651) introduced the token-limit feature and specified tokenizing each document, truncating the token list to `max_tokens_per_doc`, and applying that truncation before prompt or template assembly. This report is not a duplicate of that RFC. It concerns an implementation defect where character slicing followed by retokenization violates the token-list invariant. The same helper is used for `max_tokens_per_query`, and the reproducer demonstrates both fields directly. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
