The output above is from the container that served the failing request. Very long CPU flag/vulnerability lines were omitted because they are unrelated; full non-secret collect_env.py output can be provided if needed.
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

With Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 served by vLLM 0.27.1 using the Qwen3 reasoning parser, streaming OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, strict response_format.type=json_schema with a top-level array schema, and DSpark speculative decoding K=7, XGrammar repeatedly logged Failed to advance FSM.

Most calls completed normally, but one call returned HTTP 200 with an incomplete JSON array followed by 249,698 whitespace characters. The vLLM container remained healthy and did not restart.

This looks related to #52852, #53181, #53777 and the accepted-block validation discussed in #52452, but this report adds a separately observed environment and a preserved client-visible failure mode: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, DSpark K=7, Qwen3 reasoning, explicit JSON Schema array, concurrent streaming, and a roughly 250k-character whitespace tail.

## Related issues / PRs already checked

- #43338 appears to be the same broad structured-output/speculative-decoding family, but focuses on multi-token GPT-OSS reasoning boundaries and reports Qwen3 as its working control.
- #52852 is the closest prior report: Qwen3.8 NVFP4 + streaming + XGrammar with token 271 FSM failures.
- #53181 reports recurrence after the fix referenced when #52852 was closed.
- #53777 reports a similar failure with DFlash2 and json_object.
- #52805 stops XGrammar token batches at grammar termination.
- #52452 validates speculative accepted blocks before commit, explicitly covers reasoning-boundary/grammar-termination invariants, and mentions DSpark K5 qualification.

Please close this as a duplicate if one of those fully covers this path. I am filing it because this is a new DSpark K7 + json_schema top-level array reproduction with a saved malformed response and detailed runtime statistics.

## Effective server launch

The private registry hostname is omitted. The container reports the upstream base tag shown in the environment section. The effective vLLM command was:

~~~bash
vllm serve /model/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-unsloth --served-model-name /model/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --language-model-only --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.55 --port 80 --max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 12 --max-num-batched-tokens 24576 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/model/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark-RadixArk","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
~~~

The startup wrapper maps the draft model architecture name DSparkDraftModel to Qwen3DSparkModel before exec'ing vllm serve. No vLLM Python source files are patched.

## Request shape

The real extraction text is private, so it is redacted below. This is the exact API/options/schema shape, but not yet a deterministic public minimal prompt:

~~~python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://<vllm-endpoint>/v1", api_key="<redacted>")

response_format = {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {
        "name": "business_database_extraction",
        "strict": True,
        "schema": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "field_key": {"type": "string"},
                    "value": {"type": "string"},
                    "chunk_id": {"type": "string"},
                    "confidence": {
                        "type": "number",
                        "minimum": 0,
                        "maximum": 1,
                    },
                },
                "required": [
                    "field_key",
                    "value",
                    "chunk_id",
                    "confidence",
                ],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
}

stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="/model/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "Return only JSON matching the supplied schema."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "<redacted private extraction text>"},
    ],
    max_tokens=25000,
    temperature=0.1,
    top_p=0.95,
    presence_penalty=0.5,
    stream=True,
    stop=[],
    reasoning_effort="medium",
    response_format=response_format,
    extra_body={
        "top_k": 20,
        "repetition_penalty": 1.0,
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
            "enable_thinking": True,
            "preserve_thinking": False,
        },
    },
)
~~~

No tools were requested in these calls. The top-level array schema was accepted by vLLM and normally produced valid arrays in the other calls.

## Reproduction workload

- 10 application-level runs
- concurrency: 2
- each run split the same request into 3 model calls (12, 12 and 5 expected items)
- one downstream repair call after the malformed result
- 31 total model calls in the test
- 30 primary calls used the same private source text and field definitions

The failure was intermittent: 29 primary calls were parseable; one primary call was malformed.

## Client-visible failure

The anomalous application run took 646.055 seconds. The other nine runs took 60.406 to 69.917 seconds.

For the failing second batch:

- reasoning_content length: 3,201 characters
- no literal <thinking> or </thinking> tags
- no Markdown code fences
- response_content length: 250,070 characters
- response_content.rstrip() length: 372 characters
- trailing whitespace: 249,698 characters
- the first 3 array items were complete
- the fourth item stopped immediately after the beginning of its value string
- no chunk_id, confidence, closing object/array, or remaining 8 expected items followed

Sanitized shape of the response:

~~~json
[
  {"field_key":"f13","value":"<redacted>","chunk_id":"<redacted>","confidence":0.98},
  {"field_key":"f14","value":"<redacted>","chunk_id":"<redacted>","confidence":0.95},
  {"field_key":"f15","value":"<redacted>","chunk_id":"<redacted>","confidence":0.99},
  {"field_key":"f16","value":"<redacted prefix>"
<249698 trailing whitespace characters>
~~~

Strict JSON parsing therefore failed. A later application-level repair call returned only 3 of the 12 requested items; that partial-repair acceptance is a separate downstream completeness bug, not the cause of the original malformed vLLM response.

## Server logs from the same test window

During the test window, 20 distinct request IDs emitted backend_xgrammar.py:162 Failed to advance FSM. A representative sequence was:

~~~text
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 271. Please file an issue.
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 271. Please file an issue.
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 71093. Please file an issue.
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 271. Please file an issue.
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 71093. Please file an issue.
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 271. Please file an issue.
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 4566. Please file an issue.
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 220. Please file an issue.
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 16. Please file an issue.
ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ac42b275cf469617-8f354a4e for tokens 60. Please file an issue.
[grammar_matcher.cc:612] Warning: The matcher has terminated after accepting the stop token, but is trying to accept new token with id 198.
~~~

That representative request later completed with HTTP 200. Speculative-decoding metrics were active (K=7; average draft acceptance was approximately 51.8% to 59.7%). There was no OOM and the container restart count remained zero.

Important correlation limitation: our client logs did not retain vLLM request IDs. The FSM errors and malformed response are confirmed in the same isolated test window, but I cannot prove that the representative request ID above is the exact malformed client call.

## Expected behavior

A strict json_schema request should either:

1. return JSON that validates against the schema, or
2. terminate with an explicit request/stream error.

It should not return HTTP 200 with a truncated JSON array and hundreds of thousands of whitespace characters. Once the grammar matcher accepts its stop token, later speculative tokens should not advance or corrupt the FSM.

## Controls and current status

- I have not yet run this exact workload with speculative decoding disabled.
- I have not yet tested a build containing #52452.
- I have not reproduced this through Transformers because the observed failure is in vLLM's streaming structured-output/speculative-decoding integration rather than model semantic quality.
- The prompt-level public minimal reproduction is still pending because the source text is confidential and the failure is intermittent.

Even if top-level array schemas are considered unsupported for this combination, the server currently accepts them and succeeds on most calls; an unsupported combination should fail validation explicitly rather than emit malformed output with HTTP 200.

## Questions

1. Is vLLM 0.27.1 expected to contain all fixes from #52805 for this execution path?
2. Does #52452 address this exact DSpark K7 + Qwen3 reasoning + XGrammar failure mode?
3. Is DSpark speculative decoding with streaming reasoning and strict json_schema currently supported, or should vLLM reject this combination?
4. Would maintainers prefer the full redacted malformed response and complete collect_env.py output in a follow-up attachment?

All private endpoints, credentials, database/table/file names, and business text have been removed from this report.

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary `intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu` reproduces a `VLLM::Worker` general protection fault followed by `xe` BCS engine resets on a dual Intel Arc Pro B70 system when running Qwen3-30B-A3B with TP=2 and dynamic FP8 on Ubuntu 24.04.4 HWE kernel 6.17. The same failure pattern also reproduces with our local source-built vLLM XPU image. This suggests the issue is not caused by our source build alone, but likely involves an interaction between the host stack, `xe` driver/firmware, PCIe topology, and vLLM XPU TP=2 worker initialization / ProcessGroupXCCL path. A standalone XCCL/SYCL collective sweep passes on the same host, so this does not appear to be a generic oneCCL/SYCL collective failure. ## Hardware - 2× Intel Arc Pro B70 32GB, Battlemage G31, device `8086:e223` - Z890 motherboard with PCIe switch topology - No XeLink between GPUs - `p2p_access:0` - Each B70 reports PCIe 5.0 x8 host link - `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1` used for the two B70 GPUs ## Host stack - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS - Kernel: `6.17.0-23-generic` HWE - GPU driver: in-kernel `xe` - GuC firmware: `70.44.1` - GuC firmware version 70.49.4 has been mentioned in upstream contexts as a newer candidate; we have not yet tested an upgrade. ## Containers tested ### Intel pre-built image - `intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu` - Tested digest prefix: `sha256:e961d08135a6...` Intel's published `0.17.0-xpu` validation BOM differs from our host stack. It lists Ubuntu 25.04, KMD 6.14.0, PyTorch 2.10, `vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.4`, and oneCCL 2021.15.7.8, but `collect_env.py` inside the tested `intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu` container reports oneCCL `2021.17.2-5` and `CCL_ROOT=/opt/intel/oneapi/ccl/2021.17`. ### Local source-built image Built from vLLM `Dockerfile.xpu`: - vLLM main - PyTorch 2.11 + XPU - `vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.7` - oneCCL 2021.17.2 - oneAPI 2025.3 ## Model / vLLM setup - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` - Local BF16 model path - Dynamic FP8 quantization via `--quantization fp8` - Tensor parallelism: `--tensor-parallel-size 2` Common args: ```bash --dtype float16 --quantization fp8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64 --block-size 64 --trust-remote-code ``` ## Minimal reproducer ```bash docker pull intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu docker run -d --name vllm-tp2-repro \ --device /dev/dri \ --group-add render \ --group-add video \ --network host \ --shm-size 16g \ --ipc host \ -v /path/to/Qwen3-30B-A3B:/model:ro \ -e CCL_ATL_TRANSPORT=ofi \ -e CCL_ZE_IPC_EXCHANGE=pidfd \ -e CCL_TOPO_FABRIC_VERTEX_CONNECTION_CHECK=0 \ -e ZE_FLAT_DEVICE_HIERARCHY=COMPOSITE \ -e ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1 \ -e ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:* \ -e VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu \ python3 -u -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model /model \ --dtype float16 \ --quantization fp8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max-num-seqs 64 \ --block-size 64 \ --enforce-eager \ --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 ``` ## Observed result ```text traps: VLLM::Worker[...] general protection fault traps: VLLM::Worker[...] general protection fault xe 0000:03:00.0: [drm] GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=bcs xe 0000:07:00.0: [drm] GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=bcs ``` In one run, the GP fault was reported in `libc.so.6` from the worker processes. We do not know whether this indicates a pthread/context issue, memory corruption surfacing in libc, or another native runtime issue. ## Test matrix | Test | Stack | Key config | Result | BCS reset | |---|---|---|---|---:| | Profile A | local source-build | `CCL_ENABLE_SYCL_KERNELS=0` | Stable, `HEALTH=200`, ~362 tok/s @ 50 concurrency | 0 | | Profile B | local source-build | `CCL_ENABLE_SYCL_KERNELS=1` | XCCL / worker-init crash | yes | | Test F | local source-build | `CCL_ENABLE_SYCL_KERNELS=1`, `UR_L0_V2_FORCE_DISABLE_COPY_OFFLOAD=1` | `ProcessGroupXCCL::allreduce_impl` crash | 0 | | Test G | local source-build | above + `CCL_ALLREDUCE=ring` | Passed allreduce-init, later crashed during Dynamo/Inductor compile | 0 | | C4 v2 | local source-build | above + `--enforce-eager`, `VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=0` | `HEALTH=200`, inference works, but ~0.5 tok/s | 0 | | C8 | `intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu` | Intel image, TP=2 FP8 | `VLLM::Worker` GP fault + BCS reset | yes | | C8b | `intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu` | above + `CCL_TOPO_FABRIC_VERTEX_CONNECTION_CHECK=0` | same GP fault + BCS reset on both GPUs | yes | ## Important control: standalone XCCL/SYCL sweep passes Using the same host and relevant XPU/CCL environment as the failing vLLM path: ```bash CCL_ENABLE_SYCL_KERNELS=1 torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 xccl_sweep.py ``` Results: | Collective | fp32 | fp16 | bf16 | int32 | Max size | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | all_reduce | OK | OK | OK | OK | 33M elements / 134 MB | | all_gather | OK | OK | OK | OK | 33M elements / 134 MB | | reduce_scatter | OK | OK | OK | not tested | 33M elements / 134 MB | This suggests the hardware and base oneCCL/SYCL collective path are functional in isolation. The crash appears to require the vLLM TP=2 worker-init / ProcessGroupXCCL context. ## Failure domains observed We observed three separate failure domains while trying to make the source-built image start with `CCL_ENABLE_SYCL_KERNELS=1`. ### 1. BCS engine reset / Level Zero V2 copy-offload side effect `UR_L0_V2_FORCE_DISABLE_COPY_OFFLOAD=1` avoided the BCS engine reset in one worker-init canary, but did not fix the underlying vLLM/XCCL crash. ### 2. oneCCL topo allreduce / ProcessGroupXCCL path The source-build crashed in: ```text c10d::ProcessGroupXCCL::allreduce_impl c10d::ProcessGroupXCCL::collective c10d::ops::allreduce_XPU ``` `CCL_ALLREDUCE=ring` got past this stage, but performance collapsed and the next failure occurred later during compile. oneCCL documents that for GPU buffers, `topo` is the default algorithm, and that algorithms other than `topo` copy GPU-buffer data to host and follow the specified CPU algorithm. That likely explains the large performance drop with `CCL_ALLREDUCE=ring`. ### 3. vLLM compile / XPU graph path After bypassing the allreduce failure with `UR_L0_V2_FORCE_DISABLE_COPY_OFFLOAD=1` and `CCL_ALLREDUCE=ring`, the next failure occurred during Dynamo/Inductor compile. Adding: ```bash --enforce-eager VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=0 ``` allowed vLLM to reach `HEALTH=200` and serve inference, but throughput was only ~0.5 tok/s in our smoke test. This is a debug path, not a usable workaround. ## Stable fallback on our current host The only stable and usable config we found on this Ubuntu 24.04.4 / HWE 6.17 host is: ```bash CCL_ENABLE_SYCL_KERNELS=0 CCL_TOPO_FABRIC_VERTEX_CONNECTION_CHECK=0 SYCL_UR_USE_LEVEL_ZERO_V2=0 CCL_ATL_TRANSPORT=ofi CCL_ZE_IPC_EXCHANGE=pidfd ZE_FLAT_DEVICE_HIERARCHY=COMPOSITE ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1 ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:* VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH=1 ``` Observed performance: - ~29 tok/s single-stream - ~240 tok/s at 16 concurrency - ~362 tok/s at 50 concurrency ## Why this looks host-stack related We are not claiming the exact root cause is known. However: 1. Intel's pre-built `intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu` image reproduces the same failure pattern. 2. Adding `CCL_TOPO_FABRIC_VERTEX_CONNECTION_CHECK=0` removes the CCL topology warning but does not prevent the GP fault + BCS reset. 3. Standalone torchrun XCCL/SYCL collective sweeps pass on the same host. 4. The failure requires the vLLM TP=2 worker initialization / ProcessGroupXCCL context. 5. Our host differs from Intel's published `0.17.0-xpu` validation BOM, especially OS/kernel/KMD/firmware. A public external report claims that a similar 2× Intel Arc Pro B70 + Qwen3-30B-A3B + TP=2 + FP8 setup using `intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu` on Ubuntu 25.10 reaches high throughput. We have not reproduced that environment yet, so we treat this only as motivation for a host-stack A/B test. We are preparing a separate Ubuntu 25.10 spare-disk test and will report back. ## Hardware behavior and safety We observed BCS engine resets across multiple failed test runs. After each: - The `xe` driver recovered the engine. - GPU devices remained accessible. - Temperatures returned to idle. - No cascading errors were observed. - A full reboot cleared all state cleanly. Because BCS engine resets are not normal operation, we stopped repeated default Profile B testing on the current host stack. ## Related upstream / external signals - Intel's `0.17.0-xpu` release notes say the container is validated on Intel Arc Pro B-Series Graphics and list the validation BOM as Ubuntu 25.04 + KMD 6.14.0 + oneAPI 2025.3.2 hotfix + PyTorch 2.10 + `vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.4` + oneCCL 2021.15.7.8. - oneCCL docs state that `CCL_ALLREDUCE=topo` is the default for GPU buffers, and that non-topo algorithms copy GPU-buffer data to host and use the CPU algorithm. - Intel SYCL runtime docs state that the Level Zero V2 adapter is used by default on Xe2/Battlemage, and that `SYCL_UR_USE_LEVEL_ZERO_V2=0` selects the legacy adapter. - `vllm-xpu-kernels` tracks ongoing work to make `torch.compile` the default execution path for XPU. This may be relevant to the later Dynamo/Inductor failure domain, but the primary C8/C8b failure happens earlier during worker initialization. - There are similar multi-GPU Intel XPU reports in adjacent projects where single-GPU works but multi-GPU fails in SYCL/Level Zero cross-device paths. This may not be the same bug, but it suggests this class of issue is worth investigating. ## Questions 1. Is dual Arc Pro B70 + Qwen3-30B-A3B + TP=2 + FP8 expected to work with `intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu` on Ubuntu 24.04.4 HWE 6.17? 2. Is Ubuntu 24.04.4 / HWE 6.17 a supported host stack for `intel/vllm:0.17.0-xpu` on Intel Arc Pro B70? 3. Which host BOM should users target for dual Arc Pro B70 + Qwen3-30B-A3B + TP=2 + dynamic FP8? 4. Should this be routed to vLLM, vllm-xpu-kernels, oneCCL, Intel compute-runtime / Level Zero, or the Linux `xe` KMD? 5. What additional logs would be useful? We can provide redacted: - full `dmesg -T` - `journalctl -k -b` - docker logs - XCCL sweep script and output - `lspci -nn` - `sycl-ls` - `xpu-smi` output - exact container command lines ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [CI Failure]: (MI355) Core Operation Kernels Shard 1: kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope
body:
### Name of failing test

```
kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-False]
kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-True]
kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-64-False]
```

### Basic information

- [ ] Flaky test — **no**, fails deterministically on every attempt, including in-build retries
- [ ] Can reproduce locally — no MI355 hardware available to me; reproduced only in CI
- [ ] Caused by external libraries — no, the failure is in vLLM code

### 🧪 Describe the failing test

`(MI355) Core Operation Kernels Shard 1` fails on ROCm only. The same test file passes on `(H200 MIG 35GB) Core Operation Kernels Shard *`, and MI355 shards 2 and 3 are green — only shard 1 receives `kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py`.

```
FAILED kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-False] - IndexError: tuple index out of range
FAILED kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-0-True]  - IndexError: tuple index out of range
FAILED kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py::test_concat_mla_q_fp8_nope_and_rope[True-64-False] - IndexError: tuple index out of range
3 failed, 1164 passed, 168 skipped, 24 warnings in 1072.49s (0:17:52)
```

Traceback (from the nightly `main` build, Buildkite #90376):

```
kernels/test_concat_mla_q.py:177:
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py:134: in forward
    return self._forward_method(*args, **kwargs)
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:1561: in forward
    decode_q, _ = quant_fn(self, decode_q_flat, scale, scale_ub)
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:159: in forward_hip
    return self.forward_cuda(x, scale, scale_ub)

self = _DecodeConcatQuantFP8()
decode_ql_nope = tensor([[  24.8750,  276.0000, ...]], device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
decode_q_pe = tensor(0.3000, device='cuda:0'), scale = None, scale_ub = None

    def forward(
        self,
        decode_ql_nope: torch.Tensor,
        decode_q_pe: torch.Tensor,
        scale: torch.Tensor,
        scale_ub: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
>       if decode_q_pe.shape[-1] == 0 and decode_ql_nope.is_contiguous():
E       IndexError: tuple index out of range

/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:1556: IndexError
```

#### Root cause: the HIP fallback re-enters the subclass override

`_DecodeConcatQuantFP8` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:1540-1568`) builds all three of its forward methods from one factory, so every method has the 4-argument signature `(decode_ql_nope, decode_q_pe, scale, scale_ub)`:

```python
forward_native = _make_forward(QuantFP8.forward_native)
forward_cuda = _make_forward(QuantFP8.forward_cuda)
forward_hip = _make_forward(QuantFP8.forward_hip)
```

`QuantFP8.forward_hip` ends with a fallback to the CUDA implementation (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/input_quant_fp8.py:159`):

```python
# Fallback to CUDA implementation
return self.forward_cuda(x, scale, scale_ub)
```

On `_DecodeConcatQuantFP8`, `self.forward_cuda` is the *wrapped* 4-argument method, not `QuantFP8.forward_cuda`. So the 3-argument fallback call re-enters the wrapper with arguments shifted by one: `decode_q_pe` binds to the per-tensor `scale` (a 0-dim tensor, `tensor(0.3000)`), and `decode_q_pe.shape[-1]` raises `IndexError`.

CUDA never re-dispatches, which is why only the ROCm lane fails. On MI355 the AITER early-return branches in `forward_hip` are not taken for this configuration, so the fallback path is reached.

A minimal fix is to call the base implementation unbound, so the fallback cannot re-enter a subclass override with a different signature:

```python
return QuantFP8.forward_cuda(self, x, scale, scale_ub)
```

I have not opened a PR for this — I have no MI355 hardware to verify a fix, and I would rather leave it to the ROCm/attention owners than push an unverified change through CI.

### 📝 History of failing test

First red MI355 shard 1 today was Buildkite #90366 at 05:26Z. The guard line that raises (`if decode_q_pe.shape[-1] == 0 and decode_ql_nope.is_contiguous():`) was introduced by **#57458 "[Perf][Attention] Reduce GLM sparse MLA preparation overhead"** (merge commit `a369a7bec`, merged 2026-09-22T00:24:26Z), which is ~5 h before the first observed failure.

Note the underlying re-dispatch is older than #57458 — before it, the wrapper's first statement was `torch.cat((decode_ql_nope, decode_q_pe), dim=-1)`, which would also fail on a 0-dim tensor. #57458 changed the symptom to `IndexError`, and the failure is what surfaced the latent dispatch bug.

Every finished `(MI355) Core Operation Kernels Shard 1` run I checked on 2026-09-22 is red, across unrelated PRs and on `main`:

| Build | Trigger | Shard 1 | Shards 2 / 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#90366](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90366) | PR #58069 | fail, 2 attempts | pass |
| [#90376](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90376) | **`Full CI run - nightly` (`main`, no PR)** | fail, 2 attempts | pass |
| [#90377](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90377) | PR #49953 | fail, 2 attempts | pass |
| [#90380](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90380) | PR #56252 | fail, 3 attempts | pass |
| [#90388](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90388) | PR #55721 | fail, 2 attempts | pass |
| [#90390](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90390) | PR #57945 | fail, 2 attempts | pass |

The nightly `main` build #90376 has no PR attached and reproduces the failure with an identical log (same three parametrisations, same `mla_attention.py:1556`, `3 failed, 1164 passed`), so this is not caused by any of the PRs above.

Retrying does not help — several of the builds above show 2-3 attempts on the same job, all failed. The step has no `soft_fail`, so it blocks the `buildkite/ci/pr` rollup for every PR whose diff matches the step's `source_file_dependencies` (which include `vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/` and `tests/kernels/core`).

### CC List.

@GirasoleY @ZJY0516 (#57458), @LucasWilkinson @MatthewBonanni (`/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention` owners), @tjtanaa @dllehr-amd (ROCm)

title: [Bug]: cu129-nightly image ships torch 2.14.0+cu130 with cu129 torchvision/torchaudio, vllm serve dies on 'operator torchvision::nms does not exist'
body:
### Your current environment

Image `vllm/vllm-openai:cu129-nightly` as published on 2026-09-14 (tag `cu129-nightly-dc36fcce902a63eab06c1b93a5c4a5ee178a0c56`, digest `sha256:e756ef831f09b7486420005c5bce7a028df9b6b68d77ed7b5e9020ac7aea7e01`, buildkite release-v2 build 6550). Host: Ubuntu, driver 615.71.09, 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120). Inside the image:

```
vllm        0.29.1rc1.dev47+gdc36fcce9
torch       2.14.0+cu130
torchvision 0.28.0+cu129
torchaudio  2.11.0+cu129
triton      3.8.0
CUDA_VERSION=12.9.1 (image env)
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`vllm serve` (any model) dies at import in the `cu129-nightly` image because torch is a **cu130** wheel while torchvision and torchaudio are **cu129** wheels built against torch 2.13:

```
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/library.py", line 496, in impl
    @torch.library.register_fake("torchvision::nms")
RuntimeError: operator torchvision::nms does not exist
```

`python3 -c "import torchvision.ops"` fails the same way; `import torchaudio` then reports "PyTorch has CUDA version 13.0 whereas TorchAudio has CUDA version 12.9".

Workaround that makes the image serve (verified with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, TP=2):

```
pip install --no-deps torchvision==0.29.0+cu130 torchaudio==2.11.0+cu130 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130
```

So either the cu129 nightly picked up a cu130 torch by mistake, or torchvision/torchaudio were not bumped with it. Expected: the `cu129-nightly` tag ships a consistent cu129 torch/torchvision/torchaudio set (or, if cu130 is intended, matching vision/audio wheels).

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description The `hunyuan_a13b` reasoning parser returns different content for streaming and non-streaming Chat Completions when given the same well-formed model output: ```text ink answer ``` Non-streaming returns `reasoning="ink"` and `content="answer"`. Streaming returns the same reasoning but aggregates to `content="answer\n"`, exposing Hunyuan's closing framing marker to the client. Both requests succeed with HTTP 200 and contain exactly the same generated token IDs. Streaming clients receive model protocol syntax in the user-visible answer, while non-streaming clients receive clean content for the same tokens. Applications that render, persist, compare, or parse streamed answers can therefore expose the marker or produce mode-dependent results. ## Reproduction The Hunyuan-A13B checkpoint is over 150 GiB and is not needed to reproduce a frontend parsing bug. The included debug logits processor forces the exact token sequence documented by `HunyuanA13BReasoningParser`, while the official Hunyuan tokenizer supplies the corresponding text. The requests still go through a real vLLM engine, HTTP server, Chat Completions serving code, and the production `hunyuan_a13b` parser. Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32508930/repro_hunyuan.py), first download only the Hunyuan tokenizer files: ```bash python repro.py --prepare-tokenizer ./hunyuan_tokenizer ``` Start vLLM 0.29.0: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ PYTHONPATH="$PWD" \ VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \ VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --tokenizer ./hunyuan_tokenizer \ --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --reasoning-parser hunyuan_a13b \ --logits-processors repro:HunyuanTraceLogitsProcessor \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8033 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \ --max-model-len 256 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --enforce-eager \ 2>&1 | tee server.log ``` Run the client: ```bash python repro.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8033 \ 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The script sends the same forced output once with `stream=false` and once with `stream=true, stream_interval=1`. It exits with status 1 when the marker leak is reproduced. ## Actual result The server returns the following identical token sequence for both requests: ```text [14023, 771, 397, 771, 198, 524, 27963, 397, 27, 9399, 397, 9399, 198, 524, 9399, 29] ``` The Hunyuan tokenizer decodes it as: ```text ink answer ``` The parsed responses differ: | Mode | HTTP | `reasoning` | Aggregated `content` | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Non-streaming | 200 | `"ink"` | `"answer"` | | Streaming | 200 | `"ink"` | `"answer\n"` | The complete SSE chunks and non-streaming response are in [reproducer_hunyuan.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32508958/reproducer_hunyuan.log). The server startup and both successful requests are in [server_hunyuan.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32508963/server_hunyuan.log). ## Expected result Streaming and non-streaming parsing of the same generated token sequence should agree: ```text reasoning = "ink" content = "answer" ``` The closing `\n` frame should be consumed by the parser and must not appear in user-visible content. ## Root cause The Hunyuan streaming parser is a three-state envelope parser: `idle -> think -> response -> idle`. It is designed to keep receiving tokens in the `response` state until it recognizes [`response_end_ids`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/reasoning/hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py#L59-L64) and suppresses the closing marker. The outer `DelegatingParser` interprets the intermediate `response` state as a permanent end of reasoning: 1. After parsing `\n\n\n`, the Hunyuan parser changes its state to `response` and starts waiting for `\n` ([state transitions](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/reasoning/hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py#L177-L203)). 2. Its [`is_reasoning_end()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/reasoning/hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py#L81-L82) returns `True` in that state. 3. `DelegatingParser.parse_delta()` therefore sets [`state.reasoning_ended = True`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py#L835-L857). 4. With no tool parser configured, later deltas take the outer [content passthrough branch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py#L917-L927) and are emitted verbatim. The inner Hunyuan state machine never receives the later `response_end_ids`, so it cannot consume `\n`. The non-streaming regex sees the complete frame and removes the marker correctly. ## Related issues The unified `DelegatingParser.parse_delta()` flow was introduced by [#39446](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39446). The bug is an interface mismatch between that outer binary reasoning/content handoff and Hunyuan's three-state envelope parser. [#52658](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52658) is an open Rust frontend port of the Hunyuan A13B parser. Its implementation suppresses the closing answer marker, but it does not modify or fix the Python frontend path reproduced here. [#54499](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54499) fixes a separate `IndexError` when a partial Hunyuan response-start sequence diverges. It does not change the response-state handoff or closing-marker handling. The same Python parser behavior remains on the current `main` branch at the time of writing. Searches for Hunyuan with ``, `response_end_ids`, and streaming found no dedicated issue or fix for this leak. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [torch.compile] config hashing refactor follow-ups
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

### MOTIVATION.

[PR #26468](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/26468) moved vLLM config hashing toward an opt-out model so new compilation-relevant config fields are less likely to be accidentally omitted from torch.compile cache keys. 

This issue tracks the follow-ups and to-dos.

## TODOs
1. Refactor all locations of `compute_hash` to `compile_factors`.  `compute_hash` isn’t the right name because real computation of the hash is actually done by `utils.hash_factors`.
2. before calling `normalize value` in `get_compile_factors`, it needs to check if .compile_factors exists on the subobject. This allows us to avoid handling `PassConfig` specially as in the case for compilation.py 
4. Uniform use of `normalize_value` & `hash_factors` across configs with a compute_hash function.
5. address this comment: [comment here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/26468#discussion_r2545031784)
6. Create a shared helper instead of inlining both `_compute_code_hash` and `compilation_config_hash_factors`
7. Refactor all locations of `compute_hash` to `compile_factors`
8. Follow up on docstrings not being up-to date in the opt-out configs
9. typing cleanups (e.g., return {} where configs don’t affect graphs; use Path for traced files; consistent DP hash validation.

always print hashed configs into cache_key_factors.json

title: [Misc]: CMake Clean-up / Refactor Tasks
body:
In an effort to make the CMake more readable, stable and easy to use we have a few tasks we'd like to work on, creating a GitHub issue here to track that progress, some planned changes/investigations:

- [ ] Rename `define_gpu_extension_target`, currently this is used for CPU extensions too so the name is now misleading
- [ ] Add a CI test of local builds, i.e. `pip install -e .`
- [ ]  Warn that PTX builds are not currently supported (post https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8845), currently if there is a `+PTX` in `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` this will be ignored. We should warn when this is the case. Alternatively we can add support for PTX builds although this is generally not desirable since PTX increases the wheel size by quite a bit (PTX is larger than SASS), and we already build for all currently supported arches.
- [ ]  Have vllm-flash-attn use [ExternalProject](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/module/ExternalProject.html) currently vllm-flash-attn uses the parent CMake scope which creates many footguns since it is in a separate repo, using `ExternalProject` will mean that the vllm-flash-attn will be run in a separate CMake scope/process
  - [ ] It might be even better to revert to the FlashMLA approach, where CMake code lives in vllm.
- [ ] Look into removing early returns in CMakeLists.txt (potentially move backends into its own files)
- [ ] Potential build both C++ and CUDA extensions when building for CUDA and using torch dispatcher to dispatch between the two, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8424

title: GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next): no SM120 sparse-MLA path for rope-free MLA (qk_rope_head_dim=0) — three failure modes on RTX PRO 6000
body:
### Summary

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`) cannot start on **SM120** (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, compute 12.0) with the dedicated `glm53-flash` image: the architecture's **rope-free sparse MLA** (`qk_rope_head_dim: 0`) has no working attention/KV path on this capability. Three distinct failure modes below, ending at an explicit kernel shape guard. Weight loading itself is clean (including a quantized checkpoint — Marlin NvFp4 auto-selected), so this is purely the sparse-MLA attention/KV-cache lane.

### Environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash-x86_64-cu130@sha256:2e771fa615452282cc331eb418b3ef21636fce355bea0491fca89e6d362ab703` (engine banner: `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`; per-model image published for #53906)
- GPUs: 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (96 GB, **SM120 / compute 12.0**), driver 595.71.05, host CUDA 13.2, TP=4
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` — text config `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_nope_head_dim=256`, **`qk_rope_head_dim=0`**, `index_topk=2048` (34 linear-attention + 11 DSA layers)
- Checkpoint under test: local weight-only NVFP4 (compressed-tensors, routed experts only; attention/vision/MTP in BF16). The failures below are independent of weight quantization — they occur in backend selection / KV-cache paths before or regardless of quantized GEMMs.
- Args: `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 256 --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` (no speculative config)

### Failure mode 1 — default (`kv_cache_dtype=auto`, also explicit `fp8_e4m3`)

Engine init reaches CUDA-graph memory profiling, then the MLA cache write asserts:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'concat_and_cache_mla,
/workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu:866, pe_dim must be 64 for fp8_ds_mla'
```

`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` requires the packed `fp8_ds_mla` layout (explicit `fp8_e4m3` is normalized into it), whose cache-write kernel hardcodes the DeepSeek entry shape (512 NoPE + 64 RoPE). Rope-free MLA (pe_dim 0) violates it.

### Failure mode 2 — `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16`

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with AttentionSelectorConfig(
  head_size=512, dtype=torch.bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=bfloat16, use_mla=True, use_sparse=True, ...)
Reasons: {TRITON_MLA: [sparse not supported],
          FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120: [kv_cache_dtype not supported, kv_cache_dtype not supported]}
```

Note the bf16-capable no-rope lane (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, which explicitly whitelists `qk_nope_head_dim=256 / kv_lora_rank=512` per its `supports_combination`) is never considered: `platforms/cuda.py::_get_backend_priorities` hardcodes the `major == 12` MLA candidates to `[TRITON_MLA, FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120]`.

### Failure mode 3 — experimentally widening the SM100 no-rope lane to SM120

To test whether the gap is routing-only, we injected a runtime patch (sitecustomize) that (a) appends `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` to the SM120 candidate list and (b) widens `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMBackend.supports_compute_capability` to `{10, 12}`. The lane is then selected, all 120 shards load cleanly, and init stops at a precise shape guard:

```
ValueError: SM120 sparse MLA v32/GLM expects kv_lora_rank=512, qk_rope_head_dim=64,
and query head dim 576; got kv_lora_rank=512, qk_rope_head_dim=0, query dim=512
```

i.e. the SM120 sparse-MLA kernel path exists only for the DeepSeek-shaped (rope-64 / query-576) case; the rope-free GLM shape (query 512) has no SM120 kernel.

### Ask

Either extend the no-rope (`qk_nope=256 / kv_lora=512`) sparse-MLA support that ships for SM100 to SM120 (kernel + `supported_kv_cache_dtypes` + the hardcoded candidate list in `platforms/cuda.py`), or document `glm5_next` as unsupported on SM120 in the model's serving notes so consumer/workstation Blackwell users don't chase configuration fixes for a kernel gap.

Happy to test candidate images/patches quickly — we have a 4× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) TP4 environment with the model staged and can boot-verify within minutes. Full boot logs for all three modes available on request.

title: [Bug]: Partial cache events can reference unreported parent hashes
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... ============================== System Info ============================== OS : macOS 26.3.2 (arm64) GCC version : Could not collect Clang version : 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102) CMake version : version 4.3.2 Libc version : N/A ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : None ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.14.7 (v3.14.7:823f0323ee6, Aug 5 2026, 07:07:01) [Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : macOS-26.3.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O ============================== CPU Info ============================== Apple M5 Pro ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] numpy==2.4.6 [pip3] pyzmq==27.2.0 [pip3] torch==2.11.0 [pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0 [pip3] torchcodec==0.16.0 [pip3] torchvision==0.26.0 [pip3] transformers==5.17.0 [conda] Could not collect ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : Could not collect vLLM Version : 0.25.1.dev26+g08dfd6861 (git sha: 08dfd6861) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: Could not collect ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Hi, I believe I found a case where a BlockStored event for a partial block references a parent_block_hash that was never emitted. This prevents an external consumer from reconstructing the prefix chain. Consider a request having 1,800 tokens (so 1,536 + 128 + 128 + 8), and its tokens to be stored in a contiguous array `tokens`, and a Hashing function `H` (to simplify notation): The relevant chain is: `H1536 -> H1664 -> H1792` The problem is, we don’t emit a KV cache event for `H1664`. That is, an event is emitted only for the full block `H1536`, and for the final partial block hash `H1792`. However, we never received `H1664`, and we cannot decipher H1792’s position in the prefix chain without `H1664`. Our KV cache chain is thus irremediably broken. Code for full reproduction: ```python import json def test_partial_kv_event_parent_is_reconstructable(): hash_block_size = 128 block_size = 1536 partial_boundary = 1792 token_ids = list(range(1800)) req = make_request( "partial-parent-reproducer", token_ids, hash_block_size, sha256, ) pool = BlockPool( num_gpu_blocks=2, enable_caching=True, hash_block_size=hash_block_size, enable_kv_cache_events=True, ) blocks = pool.get_new_blocks(2) pool.cache_full_blocks( request=req, blocks=blocks, num_cached_blocks=0, num_full_blocks=1, block_size=block_size, kv_cache_group_id=0, ) pool.cache_partial_block( request=req, block=blocks[1], num_tokens=partial_boundary, kv_cache_group_id=0, block_size=block_size, ) events = [ event for event in pool.take_events() if isinstance(event, BlockStored) ] def external_hash(num_tokens): return kv_cache_utils.maybe_convert_block_hash( boundary_hash(req, hash_block_size, num_tokens) ) h1536 = external_hash(1536) h1664 = external_hash(1664) h1792 = external_hash(1792) names = { h1536: "H1536", h1664: "H1664", h1792: "H1792", None: None, } for event in events: print( json.dumps( { "block_hashes": [ names.get(h, repr(h)) for h in event.block_hashes ], "parent_block_hash": names.get( event.parent_block_hash, repr(event.parent_block_hash), ), "token_range": [ event.token_ids[0], event.token_ids[-1] + 1, ], "token_count": len(event.token_ids), "block_size": event.block_size, } ) ) assert events[0].block_hashes == [h1536] assert events[0].parent_block_hash is None assert events[1].block_hashes == [h1792] assert events[1].parent_block_hash == h1664 assert events[1].token_ids == token_ids[1664:1792] emitted_hashes = { block_hash for event in events for block_hash in event.block_hashes } skipped_context_reconstructs_parent = ( getattr(events[1], "skipped_parent_block_hash", None) == h1536 and getattr(events[1], "skipped_token_ids", None) == token_ids[1536:1664] ) assert h1664 in emitted_hashes or skipped_context_reconstructs_parent, ( "H1792 references H1664, but H1664 was not emitted and the event " "contains no skipped ancestry from H1536" ) ``` Which produces: ``` {"block_hashes":["H1536"],"parent_block_hash":null,"token_range":[0,1536],"token_count":1536,"block_size":1536} {"block_hashes":["H1792"],"parent_block_hash":"H1664","token_range":[1664,1792],"token_count":128,"block_size":128} ``` i.e., we get `H1792`, but its parent `H1664` was never emitted. PR #44488 provides a hint on fixing the issue, by introducing the `skipped_parent_block_hash` param in `BlockStored` events. I have an initial attempt [here](https://github.com/Lucas-Fernandes-Martins/vllm/compare/efc443a645f4986bc2f458d74ebf841e158a4813...1b2e19ed69) to use `skipped_parent_block_hash` to solve the issue, adding those fields to `cache_partial_block` by producing instead: ```json { "block_hashes": ["H1536"], "parent_block_hash": null, "token_ids": "tokens[0:1536]", "block_size": 1536 } { "block_hashes": ["H1792"], "parent_block_hash": "H1664", "token_ids": "tokens[1664:1792]", "block_size": 128, "skipped_parent_block_hash": "H1536", "skipped_token_ids": "tokens[1536:1664]", "skipped_extra_keys": [null] } ``` Thank you very much and let me know if I can tackle this issue! ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug] MTP draft model does not inherit --hf-overrides (YaRN): length gate + dummy-0 drafts silently kill speculative acceptance beyond the draft's max_model_len
body:
# [Bug] MTP draft model does not inherit `--hf-overrides` (YaRN): length gate + dummy-0 drafts silently kill speculative acceptance beyond the draft's `max_model_len`

## Summary

When a model's context is extended with `--hf-overrides` **as a dict** (e.g. YaRN ×4), the MTP draft model's `model_config` is **not** given the override — `compose_draft_hf_overrides()` documents dict overrides as "target-specific key patches and are not applied to the draft". The draft therefore keeps the model's native `max_position_embeddings` as its `max_model_len`.

That length feeds the drafter's input gate in `gpu_model_runner` (`_input_fits_in_drafter`): once the batch's longest sequence + `num_spec_tokens` exceeds the **draft's** `max_model_len`, vLLM **skips draft proposal entirely and substitutes dummy token 0 for every request in the batch**. Since `rejection_sampler` reserves only `-1` as placeholder, token 0 is an ordinary token and is "accepted" only when the target happens to sample 0 — ≈0%. Result: engine-wide MTP acceptance collapses to ~0 (per-position 0.000/0.000) for as long as any sequence is past the boundary, each decode step still pays the target-side cost of verifying the dummies, and the only signal is the spec-decode metrics. Target output stays correct; nothing is logged.

Note (correction to earlier text in this issue): the RoPE objects themselves are **not** what diverges — the MTP layer builds its rope from the target's config (`initialize_model` never forwards the draft `model_config` to the model class, and `qwen3_5_mtp` reads `vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config`). What diverges is the **draft's `max_model_len`**, which drives the gate. Thanks to @jahnclawdmonet for tracing this.

## Environment

- vLLM **0.26.0** (V1 engine), image `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` (commit ffb2d59b1c05); code paths verified in-container at the line numbers below, same code reported on main
- Model: `Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` — Qwen3-Next-style **hybrid GDN** (48 linear-attention GDN layers + 16 full-attention layers + 1 MTP draft layer), fp8 weights, fp8 KV cache
- Hardware: 2× NVIDIA H20 96 GB, `--tensor-parallel-size 2`
- Key flags: `--max-model-len 1000000`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--enable-chunked-prefill`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--reasoning-parser qwen3`, and:

```
--hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"rope_parameters":{"mrope_interleaved":true,"mrope_section":[11,11,10],"rope_type":"yarn","rope_theta":10000000,"partial_rotary_factor":0.25,"factor":4.0,"original_max_position_embeddings":262144}}}'
```

(i.e. YaRN ×4: native 262,144 → 1,000,000 max sequence length.)

## Mechanism (verified in v0.26.0 source)

1. `vllm/config/speculative.py`, `compose_draft_hf_overrides()`: dict overrides are not applied to the draft. Startup logs accordingly show
   - target: `Using max model len 1000000`, `rope_type=yarn, factor=4.0`
   - **MTP draft: `Using max model len 262144`** (native config)
2. The draft's rope is *not* the mismatch: `initialize_model` (`vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py:63`) passes only `vllm_config` to new-style model classes — the draft `model_config` parameter is accepted but never forwarded; `qwen3_5_mtp.py:70,73` reads `vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config` (the target's, overridden config), and `_ROPE_DICT` (`rotary_embedding/__init__.py:30,83`) hands the MTP layers the target's rope object itself.
3. The gate: `gpu_model_runner.py:665-669` sets `effective_drafter_max_model_len = draft_config.max_model_len`; `_input_fits_in_drafter` (`:4481-4493`) returns `common_attn_metadata.max_seq_len + num_spec_tokens <= effective_drafter_max_model_len` (MTP: `+2`, no DFlash bonus). `max_seq_len` is the **batch's** longest total sequence (prompt + generated, counted optimistically).
4. On gate failure: `:4601` skips `propose_draft_token_ids`; `:4647-4654` substitutes `torch.zeros(...).expand(len(req_ids), num_spec_tokens)` — dummy token 0 for **every request in the batch** (the in-code comment cites protecting Mamba recurrent state from stale drafts).
5. `rejection_sampler.py:30`: `PLACEHOLDER_TOKEN_ID = -1` is reserved — token 0 is ordinary. A dummy survives only if the target's argmax is 0 (greedy kernel) or the random kernel samples token 0 at its own probability: ≈0, without being structurally 0.
6. Batch-wide dead regime: because the gate reads the batch maximum and the dummy expansion covers all `req_ids`, **one long session holds every concurrent request in the dead regime until it finishes** — matching the observed exactly-0.000 per-position rates engine-wide, including for short requests.

### Bisection of the crossover (same engine, same request shape)

| prompt length | mean acceptance length | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 243,000 tok | 1.74 – 3.00 | healthy |
| 279,000 tok | 1.00 (0% accepted) | dead |
| 312,000 tok | 1.00 (0.05%) | dead |

The crossover sits just below 262,142 (draft `max_model_len` − 2) and slides lower as the session generates — consistent with the table (279 K prompt + a few hundred generated already crosses).

### Signature in engine logs

While a >262 K sequence decodes, the per-10 s `SpecDecoding metrics` line shows:

```
Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 tokens/s,
Drafted throughput: ~190 tokens/s, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000,
Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0%
```

while `vllm:num_requests_running`, TTFT and KV usage look normal. When the long sequence finishes, acceptance recovers to 2.5+ on its own — which initially made this look workload/load-related.

## Impact

- On a shared engine with mixed traffic, decode throughput oscillates with the longest live session: with 2 concurrent ~312 K-token agent sessions we measured engine-wide acceptance 0.05% (mean length 1.00) and ~60–90 tok/s total, vs. ~150–170 tok/s for comparable load once the draft was fixed.
- The dead regime is **batch-wide**, not per-request: all concurrent users lose the spec-decode benefit (and pay the dummy-verification cost) while any one session is past the boundary.
- Very hard to diagnose: no error/warning anywhere; target output remains correct; the only signals are the spec-decode metrics or "it got slower after our sessions grew past X tokens".

## Workaround we used (model-file hack)

Baking the rope extension into the model's `config.json` (`text_config.rope_parameters`: `rope_type=yarn, factor=4.0, original_max_position_embeddings=262144`) so the draft's native config already carries it:

- draft startup log: `Using max model len 262144` → `1048576` (derived length 262144×4, clamped to the target's 1,000,000) → the gate stops firing
- 279 K request: mean acceptance length 1.00 → 2.37–2.72
- 2×312 K concurrent: 0.05% acceptance → 2.27–2.35, 153 tok/s
- no regression below 262 K (2.30–3.00)

This works but requires editing the model distribution — a user should not have to know this.

## Suggested fix

1. **Propagate dict `hf_overrides` to the draft's `model_config`** (at least the length-affecting fields: `max_position_embeddings` / rope scaling), so the draft's `max_model_len` tracks the target's extended length and the gate stops firing. This is exactly what the `config.json` bake achieves manually.
2. At minimum, **warn at startup** when speculative decoding is enabled and `draft_model_config.max_model_len` < the target's effective `max_model_len` (i.e. the condition the gate actually uses — not the native `max_position_embeddings`). This path currently emits no log. Analogous to the existing warning at `speculative.py:901` for `num_speculative_tokens > 1`.

## Reproduction steps (minimal)

1. Serve any MTP-capable model whose native `max_position_embeddings` is smaller than the extended length, extending context with a **dict** `--hf-overrides` (e.g. YaRN), with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`.
2. Confirm startup logs show different `Using max model len` for target vs. MTP draft (draft = native).
3. Send a chat completion whose prompt token count puts the total sequence above the draft's `max_model_len` (crossover ≈ draft `max_model_len` − 2).
4. Observe `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total` stop growing (Δ≈0 while Δdrafts≈2 per step) and `Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000` — for **all** requests in the batch, not just the long one.
5. Control: same request below the threshold → acceptance healthy.

## Related (distinct) issues

- #54453 — quadratic decode under structured output + reasoning parser (CPU-side; fixed by #55223, which we also backported; not the cause of this one)
- #53912 — hybrid + MTP output corruption
- #55766 — hybrid GDN + mamba `align` + prefix-cache hit → NaN logits

This issue is a fourth, silent MTP failure mode specific to **target/draft `max_model_len` divergence** via dict `hf_overrides`; it affects any hybrid or dense model that extends context that way with MTP enabled.

title: [Bug]: CPU W4A16 Whisper fails: cpu_gemm_wna16 rejects 3-D encoder activations; packed k_proj bias is synthesized incorrectly
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 3.28.3 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cpu Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : None ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.13.15 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Aug 10 2026, 13:05:01) [GCC 14.4.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 CPU(s): 384 Vendor ID: AuthenticAMD Model name: AMD EPYC 9654 96-Core Processor Thread(s) per core: 2 Core(s) per socket: 96 Socket(s): 2 NUMA node(s): 2 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] numpy==2.4.6 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cpu [pip3] torchao==0.17.0+cpu [pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0+cpu [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0+cpu [pip3] transformers==5.15.1 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 [pip3] compressed-tensors==0.17.0 [pip3] vllm==0.27.1+cpu [pip3] zentorch==2.13.0.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : Could not collect vLLM Version : 0.27.1 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: Could not collect ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary Loading a compressed-tensors **W4A16 Whisper** checkpoint on **CPU** (`CPUWNA16LinearKernel` / `cpu_gemm_wna16`) fails at runtime. The Whisper encoder feeds **3-D** activations `[B, T, D]` into quantized Linear layers, but the C++ kernel treats the input as 2-D `[M, K]` and reads `K` from `input.size(1)`. For encoder time `T=28` that is not a multiple of 32, so the kernel aborts. Separately, packed checkpoints expose `.k_proj.weight_packed` and omit `.k_proj.bias`. `_create_fake_bias_for_k_proj` only matches `.k_proj.weight` and sizes the fake bias from `weight.size(0)`, which is wrong for packed AWQ/Marlin layouts (`d_model` is required). After the crash is avoided, that produces garbage transcripts (WER 100 on LibriSpeech in our runs). ### Repro Model: https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized.w4a16 ```python from vllm import LLM from vllm.assets.audio import AudioAsset llm = LLM( model="RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized.w4a16", device="cpu", dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=448, enforce_eager=True, limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 1}, ) prompt = "<|startoftranscript|><|en|><|transcribe|><|notimestamps|>" audio, sr = AudioAsset("mary_had_lamb").audio_and_sample_rate outputs = llm.generate( { "prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (audio, sr)}, } ) print(outputs[0].outputs[0].text) ``` ### Expected The request completes. BF16 openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo on the same CPU path is around 2.x WER on LibriSpeech; W4A16 should be in the same ballpark, not crash. ### Actual ```RuntimeError: Check failed: a_k_size % 32 == 0 (28 vs. 0)``` ### Root cause - 3-D activations. ops.cpu_gemm_wna16 does not flatten leading dims the way int4_scaled_mm_cpu already does (x.reshape(-1, x_shape[-1]), then reshape the output back). Whisper encoder Linear layers therefore pass [B, T, D] straight into the C++ op. - Packed k_proj bias. WhisperForConditionalGeneration.load_weights only walks .k_proj.weight. Compressed-tensors W4A16 checkpoints use .k_proj.weight_packed and have no real .k_proj.bias. The fused qkv_proj/kv_proj path still needs a d_model-sized zeros bias; using packed dim0 is wrong. ### Suggested fix (native vLLM) - Flatten/reshape in cpu_gemm_wna16 to match int4_scaled_mm_cpu. - In _create_fake_bias_for_k_proj, also match .k_proj.weight_packed, size the fake bias from config.d_model, and do not override a real .k_proj.bias. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Performance]: multimodal preprocessing is single-threaded per API server; a wider thread pool does not help (GIL) — process pool for _mm_executor?
body:
### Proposal to improve performance

**Summary.** For a VLM serving one image per request, the renderer's single-worker multimodal executor (`vllm/renderers/base.py`, `_mm_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)`, "must stay single-worker per #38418") is a hard wall in front of the engine, and a wider *thread* pool barely moves it: with the cache disabled (so #38418 does not apply) I widened it on a B300 host — **2 threads: +20 % render throughput (14.0 → 16.8 pages/s); 6 threads: −70 % (→ 4 pages/s), GPU starved**. The GIL, not the cache, is the constraint. Proposal: run multimodal preprocessing in a **process pool**, sized by a config value, default 1 worker as today.

### Report of performance regression

Not a regression between versions — a measurement of the executor's shape at `v0.29.0`.

**Setup.** Qwen3.5-VL-class 4B model (custom weights), 1 × B300, 8 vCPU (Modal), `--max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-queued-reqs 216 --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-enable-prefix-caching --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1}'`, `mm_processor_kwargs max_pixels=3145728`. Client: 300 simultaneous chat completions each carrying one inline 1275×1650 PNG (218 KB, ~2.1 k prompt tokens), `max_tokens = min_tokens = 1024`; then an open loop of 20 requests/s for 60 s with 16-token decodes, so the GPU drains faster than the render and the render alone sets the rate. "Pre-engine wait" is `time_to_first_token − time_in_model_prefill − time_in_queue` from the `llm_request` trace span (the time between `arrival_time` and the engine seeing the request — i.e. the renderer). A plugin replaced `_mm_executor` after `BaseRenderer.__init__` with a K-worker `ThreadPoolExecutor` (re-binding `_process_multimodal_async` / `_clear_mm_cache_async` via `make_async`) and set `set_default_torch_num_threads()`'s default to `8 // K` (also tried 8 per worker — same result).

| MM executor workers (torch intra-op threads each) | 300 at once: served p50 / p99 | pre-engine wait p50 / max | engine queue (`time_in_queue`) max | container CPU p50 (of 8 cores) | GPU util p50 | 20 rps × 60 s: pages/s served |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 (8)** — today | 17.5 s / 28.5 s | 8.0 s / 14.5 s | 9.8 s | 1.4 (6.7 in the steady run) | 58 % | **14.0** |
| 2 (4) | 17.4 s / 28.3 s | 6.7 s / 11.7 s | 12.1 s | 1.4 (6.9 in the steady run) | 57 % | **16.8** (1200/1200 served, 0 refused; p50 8.8 s vs 13.3 s) |
| 6 (1) | **29.7 s / 57.1 s** | **27.3 s / 54.2 s** | **0** | 4.4 | 60 % | **4.2** |
| 6 (8) | — | — | 0 | 3.7 | 15 % | **3.8** |

Outputs at temperature 0 were byte-identical across configurations (30 requests, image by URL and inline); no errors or crashes in any configuration — thread-safety was not the problem.

**Reading.** Two threads help a little (the second thread overlaps the first's GIL-free tensor ops). With six render threads the engine's queue never forms and GPU utilisation drops: the renderer got *slower* in aggregate, and CPU utilisation fell rather than rose. That is the GIL-convoy signature: the HF processor's torch/numpy ops release and re-acquire the GIL per op, and with K render threads plus the event loop contending, every re-acquire waits a scheduling round, so a render that takes ~70 ms alone takes seconds abreast. The single worker's ~6.7 busy cores are its own intra-op threads (which is also why going from 8 to 16 vCPUs changed nothing for the single worker in an earlier run: the ops do not scale past ~8 threads).

**Why the cache guard is not the limit here.** #38418 (closing #38375) guards the multimodal processor *cache* — the LRU/SHM sender/receiver caches are not thread-safe and assume P0's insertion order at P1 — and #49524 kept `_mm_executor` single-worker for that reason. With `--mm-processor-cache-gb 0`, `processor_cache_from_config` returns `None`, the engine core builds no receiver cache, and (with prefix caching off) `_process_mm_uuids` names every item per request; nothing is shared between requests. The remaining path is already thread-safe (`maybe_make_thread_pool`'s tokenizer copies, `AtomicCounter`). So a wider thread pool is *safe* in this configuration — it is just not faster.

**What would help.**
1. A `ProcessPoolExecutor` (or a small pool of forked/spawned preprocessing workers) for the CPU-bound part of `_process_multimodal`, sized by a config value (default 1 = today's behaviour), refused when the processor cache is enabled (the existing #38418 rule). The processed `MultiModalKwargs` would cross a process boundary once more (they already cross to the engine core), so the cost is one extra serialization of `pixel_values` per request — small against the ~70 ms render, and the GIL is per process.
2. Alternatively, `--api-server-count N` already parallelises renders across processes, but `--max-num-queued-reqs` / `--max-num-queued-tokens` are enforced per API-server process, so admission caps multiply by N; deployments that rely on those caps cannot use it as is. Making those caps global (or documenting the division) would make it a real option.

Happy to help test either on the same setup.

title: [Feature]: Bind batch-invariant mode into KV-offload namespaces and KV-connector compatibility checks
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**Summary.** `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` is not part of any KV-offload namespace or KV-connector compatibility check. An instance in batch-invariant mode can therefore load KV blocks that were produced under a different numerical configuration (non-invariant kernels, another attention backend, another GPU architecture) through a shared offload tier or a P/D transfer. Nothing signals that this happened. Its output then depends on whether a block was a hit and on which instance wrote it, which undercuts the documented promise that output is "deterministic and independent of the batch size or the order of requests in a batch".

This comes from reading the code at `v0.29.0` (98dff2a). **I have not reproduced a divergence.** I'm filing a feature request rather than a bug so it can be discussed before anyone builds a repro.

**What the code does today**

- The offload namespace is `FileMapper.fields`, which holds `model_name`, `tokens_per_hash`, `blocks_per_file`, the parallel sizes, `dtype`, `kv_cache_groups` and `inference_engine` ([file_mapper.py#L53-L64](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/v1/kv_offload/file_mapper.py#L53-L64)). The P2P tier's fingerprint is built from the same fields ([p2p/manager.py#L281-L286](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py#L281-L286)). The namespace has no batch-invariance flag, attention backend or device capability. The docs describe cross-instance sharing through a shared `root_dir` as working by default ([kv_offloading_usage.md#L155](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md#L155)).
- The NIXL compatibility hash includes `attn_backend_name`, `cache_dtype`, `vllm_version` and more, but not the batch-invariance flag ([nixl/metadata.py#L171-L190](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/metadata.py#L171-L190)). The other connectors I looked at (HF3FS, Mooncake, MoRIIO) have no model-level compatibility check.
- A grep for `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` or `batch_invariant` returns nothing under `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer`, `vllm/v1/kv_offload`, `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload` or `vllm/v1/core`. There's no warning of the kind `attention.py` emits when it disables prefix caching for FLASHINFER/TRITON_MLA under batch invariance ([attention.py#L363-L378](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py#L363-L378)).
- No test under `tests/v1/determinism/` configures a KV connector or an offload tier, so this combination isn't covered.

The same gaps are present on `main` today (88aa0d2).

**Why it matters.** The reason to enable batch invariance is reproducibility: RL rollouts versus the trainer, evals, and replay. Offload and P/D are exactly how those workloads get scaled out. A KV block written by a non-invariant producer is not the block the consumer would have computed. Recent namespace fixes such as #49438 (effective dtype) and #49440 (model runner / byte layout) close the gap for *interpretability*. This request is about *numerical provenance*, which matters only when a user has asked for determinism.

**Proposed change (small, opt-in by construction)**

1. **Offload namespace.** In `FileMapper`, add `"batch_invariant": True` to `fields` only when `envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set. That follows the pattern used for `replicated_layout`, where the field is written only when True, so existing deployments' digests are unchanged. When it is set, also add the attention backend name and the device capability, since batch-invariant bits are only reproducible within a backend and architecture. The P2P fingerprint picks this up automatically.
2. **NIXL.** Add the same factors to `compute_nixl_compatibility_hash`, again only when batch invariance is on, so mixed P/D pairs fail the handshake instead of silently mixing numerics.
3. **Connectors without a compatibility handshake.** Emit a `warning_once` when batch invariance is on and a KV connector is configured, mirroring the prefix-caching warning in `attention.py`.
4. **Docs.** Add a sentence to `batch_invariance.md` saying the guarantee covers KV transferred or offloaded only between producers with the same batch-invariance setting, backend and architecture.

I'm happy to send a PR for 1–3 if this direction looks right.

### Alternatives

- **Documentation only** (item 4). This is cheapest, but the failure stays silent.
- **Disable KV connectors under batch invariance**, as is done for prefix caching on FLASHINFER/TRITON_MLA. This is simpler but blocks the scale-out use cases above.
- **Namespace unconditionally** by backend and device. This is stricter, but it changes digests for every existing deployment and splits caches that are fine to share when determinism isn't required.

### Additional context

- The upstream offloading tests already acknowledge that the resume path isn't bit-exact for Mamba: the "not bit-exact" comment in [test_offloading_connector.py#L586-L590](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py#L586-L590). The GPU P/D accuracy tests use a 0.05 gsm8k tolerance. So nothing currently checks bitwise equality across a handoff under batch invariance.
- Related: #27433 (batch invariance tracking), #49261 and #49266 (model-revision namespace), #49438, #49440.

cc @orozery @ApostaC (kv_offload) @NickLucche (kv_transfer / NIXL) @yewentao256 (batch invariance). Sorry for the broad ping; I'm not sure which of you owns this intersection.

- [x] I searched existing issues and PRs (batch invariance with offload, connector, disaggregation and namespace) and found no duplicate.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## 🐛 Describe the bug Multi-node TP=8 (2 nodes × 4 H200) serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash hangs indefinitely during engine startup, inside `ncclCommInitRank` graph/connection phase — before weight loading begins. The hang is deterministic and reproducible across 8+ restarts with different NCCL env configurations. Launch commands (per official multiprocessing multi-node docs) Head node: ```bash vllm serve /.cache/deepseek-v41-flash \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enable-chunked-prefill \ --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \ --master-addr \ --trust-remote-code --disable-custom-all-reduce ``` Worker node: same + `--headless --node-rank 1`. Observed behavior (NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE) Both nodes bootstrap fine (TCP bootstrap OK, `commId` shared, 2 nodes detected). Then, with IB enabled: Even local_ranks (0, 2 / 4, 6) complete `Init COMPLETE`, log their `Trees`, and establish cross-node GDRDMA channels: `Channel 00/0 : 0[0] -> 4[0] [send] via NET/IB/4/GDRDMA`, `Channel 01/0 : 2[2] -> 6[2] [send] via NET/IB/5/GDRDMA` Odd local_ranks (1, 3 / 5, 7) stop after `comm 0x... rank N nRanks 8 nNodes 2 localRanks 4 localRank N MNNVL 0` + one `Trees` line — no Channel lines, no Init COMPLETE, indefinitely The APIServer loops forever on: `Waiting for 1 local, 0 remote core engine proc(s) to start.` Weight loading (`Loading safetensors`) never starts All worker threads sleep (futex / socket / ib_uverbs_event_read) — no spinning, no watchdog timeout, no error With `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (Socket transport): the same hang, but now all 8 ranks block at the `MNNVL 0` boundary with zero Channel lines. The even/odd localRank asymmetry (the most distinctive part) On both nodes, exactly cudaDev 0 and cudaDev 2 (even local_ranks) complete init and own the cross-node GDRDMA channel pairs (0↔4 on one rail, 2↔6 on another). Odd local_ranks never establish their cross-node connections (1↔5, 3↔7). The pattern is stable across restarts and independent of: Variable tested Result `NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION=8` vs default ❌ no change `NCCL_CROSS_NIC=0` vs `1` ❌ no change `NCCL_NCHANNELS_PER_NET_PEER=4` vs `8` vs unset ❌ no change (worse: all ranks block) `NCCL_MAX/MIN_NCHANNELS=16/8` vs unset ❌ no change `NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=SYS` + `NCCL_NET_GDR_READ=1` vs unset ❌ no change `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (Socket transport) ❌ all 8 ranks block (earlier) `--disable-custom-all-reduce` ❌ no change Worker `--headless` (was missing initially — fixed) ❌ no change to the even/odd pattern env propagation ✅ verified — every NCCL_* var logged as "set by environment" on both nodes Ruled out TCP connectivity: bootstrap + `distributed_init_method=tcp://...:29501` reachable from both nodes (tested live) `/dev/shm`, UID, permissions: identical on both nodes GPU-NIC topology: NV6 intra-node, NICs PIX-adjacent to their NUMA-local GPUs, GDR works (GDRDMA channels DO form for even ranks) Env propagation: NCCL TRACE confirms every var read on both nodes Same model + same topology works on SGLang (NCCL 2.28.3) with identical k8s/network setup — 4 rails, GDRDMA, TP8/EP8 Hypothesis The rank-pair channel assignment during `ncclCommInitRank` graph-connect deadlocks when ranks need to establish cross-node QP connections in an order that requires the odd-rank pair's initiator to be a rank that is itself still initializing. ## Additional context Related: #53894 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro 2-node hang — `--disable-custom-all-reduce` fixed their case, not ours), #46097 (MiniMax multi-node collective deadlock — "ranks not in the same collective instance" hypothesis), #57423 (FlashInfer autotune rank-0-only cache — ours hangs earlier, at comm init) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Installation]:  v0.30.0 CPU wheels now require manylinux_2_39 (glibc 2.39), breaking installation on Ubuntu 22.04/Rhel9
body:
### Your current environment

- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (glibc 2.35) / Rhel9.6 (glibc 2.34)
- Arch: x86_64
- Python: 3.10
- Installing: `vllm-0.30.0+cpu-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_39_x86_64.whl` from the GitHub release assets

### How you are installing vllm

```sh
pip3 install --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu "https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/download/v0.30.0/vllm-0.30.0+cpu-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_39_x86_64.whl"
```

### Description

Hi vLLM team (@khluu (release coordinator of v0.30.0), @bigPYJ1151 (reviewer of [PR49410](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49410)), @zhejiangxiaomai (author of [PR49410](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49410)), first of all, thank you for the v0.30.0 release and for continuing to ship prebuilt CPU wheels. They are very helpful for us.

We noticed that the platform tag of the CPU wheels changed between releases:

| Release | CPU wheel platform tag |
|---|---|
| v0.29.0 | `manylinux_2_34` (x86_64 / aarch64) |
| v0.30.0 | `manylinux_2_39` (x86_64 / aarch64) |

From what we can tell, this comes from `docker/Dockerfile.cpu` moving its base image from `ubuntu:22.04` (GCC 12) to `ubuntu:25.04` (GCC 15) in #49410, which was needed for the binutils >= 2.44 requirement of the new AMX-FP8 kernels. The CUDA (`manylinux_2_28`) and XPU (`manylinux_2_34`) wheels were not affected.

As a result, the official CPU wheels can no longer be installed on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (glibc 2.35) and Rhel9 (glibc 2.34). Ubuntu 22.04 is still within Canonical's standard support window (until April 2027, with ESM until 2032) and is still widely used in production and CI environments, including ours. We could not find any note in the release notes or docs indicating that dropping Ubuntu 22.04 / glibc < 2.39 support for CPU wheels was intended, so we wanted to raise it here.

### Request

Would it be possible to continue publishing a CPU wheel that is installable on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35), for example with a `manylinux_2_34` tag, alongside the new `manylinux_2_39` wheel? Some options that might work:

We would be happy to help test a candidate wheel on Ubuntu 22.04, or to contribute a PR for the build change if the maintainers agree on a direction.

Thank you for your time and for all the work on vLLM!
