title: [Bug]: GLM required tool-call grammar accepts split marker tokens that the streaming parser treats as content
body:
### Your current environment

- **vLLM:** tag [`v0.28.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/v0.28.0), commit `2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a`. Verified from the image build reference and byte-for-byte comparison of the relevant installed parser/grammar files.
- **xgrammar:** `0.2.6`.
- **vllm-ascend:** commit `c267db731d03e18042047ea1594e033673e46a6f`.
- Tokenizer: GLM-5; transformers `5.14.1`, tokenizers `0.22.2`.

The reproduction runs grammar/parser logic on CPU and needs only tokenizer files, not model weights or accelerator inference.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With GLM `tool_choice="required"`, xgrammar accepts `<tool_call>` / `</tool_call>` assembled from ordinary sub-tokens. vLLM's streaming parser only recognizes the atomic marker IDs and emits the split markers as content. A sequence can therefore satisfy the required-tool grammar while producing **zero tool calls**.

Both encodings below decode to exactly the same text, including the stop token:

```text
<tool_call>get_current_time</tool_call><|observation|>
```

#### Minimal reproduction

Save the script below as `repro.py`, then run:

```bash
python repro.py /path/to/GLM-5-tokenizer
```

This constructs token sequences with thinking enabled and a valid `</think>` boundary; it does not run model generation. `reasoning=False` on the grammar represents the tool constraint applied **after** reasoning ends.

```python
"""CPU component reproduction; only tokenizer files are needed.
Usage: python repro_glm_split_markers.py /path/to/GLM-5-tokenizer
This constructs token sequences; it does not run model generation.
"""
import sys
from collections import Counter

import xgrammar as xgr
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.parser.glm47_moe import glm47_moe_config
from vllm.parser.engine.streaming_parser_engine import StreamingParserEngine

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(sys.argv[1], trust_remote_code=True)
tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {
    "name": "get_current_time",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
}}]
# vLLM applies this tool grammar after reasoning ends.
tag = xgr.get_model_structural_tag(
    "glm_4_7", tools=tools, tool_choice="required", reasoning=False,
)
ctx = xgr.GrammarCompiler(
    xgr.TokenizerInfo.from_huggingface(tok)
).compile_structural_tag(tag)

# Captured GLM-5 encodings, with the SAME observation stop in both cases.
cases = {
    "atomic": [154843, 455, 11075, 3009, 154844, 154829],
    "split": [27, 14163, 13420, 29, 455, 11075, 3009,
              522, 14163, 13420, 29, 154829],
}
expected = "<tool_call>get_current_time</tool_call><|observation|>"
prefix = tok.encode("I need the current time.", add_special_tokens=False)
prefix += [tok.convert_tokens_to_ids("</think>")]
for label, ids in cases.items():
    assert tok.decode(ids) == expected, "Tokenizer differs from the tested GLM-5 tokenizer"
    matcher = xgr.GrammarMatcher(
        ctx, override_stop_tokens=[154820, 154827, 154829],
    )
    accepted = all(matcher.accept_token(t) for t in ids)
    engine = StreamingParserEngine(glm47_moe_config(thinking=True), tok)
    events = engine.feed(tok.decode(prefix), prefix)
    # ASCII tool text, so decoding each suffix token does not split UTF-8.
    for t in ids:
        events += engine.feed(tok.decode([t]), [t])
    events += engine.finish()
    counts = Counter(e.type.name for e in events)
    content = "".join(e.value for e in events if e.type.name == "TEXT_CHUNK")
    print(label, "grammar_accepts=", accepted,
          "reasoning_ends=", counts["REASONING_END"],
          "tool_starts=", counts["TOOL_CALL_START"],
          "tool_ends=", counts["TOOL_CALL_END"],
          "content=", repr(content))
```

Observed output:

```text
atomic grammar_accepts= True reasoning_ends= 1 tool_starts= 1 tool_ends= 1 content= ''
split grammar_accepts= True reasoning_ends= 1 tool_starts= 0 tool_ends= 0 content= '<tool_call>get_current_time</tool_call>'
```

#### Cause and expected behavior

[`StreamingParserEngine._process_lex_tokens`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a/vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py#L341) treats text-lexer matches for token-ID terminals as content once token IDs have been supplied. GLM registers its tool markers as token-ID terminals, but xgrammar accepts both encodings.

The grammar and parser should agree on valid tool-call encodings, either by constraining generation to canonical marker IDs or by recognizing the accepted encoding in the constrained tool path. Globally disabling strict parsing could misinterpret literal markup.

The same relevant parser logic is present in main at `c843f0cab78b413f2b0a5c2282cb71e3a3937b11` (source inspection only; the executed reproduction uses `v0.28.0` + xgrammar `0.2.6`).

#### Real-generation evidence boundary

A real response generated split markers, stopped normally, and returned content instead of `tool_calls`. That service had thinking enabled but no reasoning parser. Adding `--reasoning-parser glm45` while retaining thinking made 10/10 subsequent requests succeed. **We have not reproduced natural split-marker generation after correcting that configuration.** The CPU test above demonstrates the remaining encoding mismatch, not its frequency under correct configuration.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [ ] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

I searched existing issues and inspected the relevant upstream source. I have not consulted the documentation chatbot, so I am leaving the combined checkbox unchecked.

title: [Rust Frontend][RFC] Request tracing for the Rust frontend
body:
## Motivation

The Rust frontend has no OpenTelemetry tracing, and `--otlp-traces-endpoint` is rejected at startup. Given an OTLP endpoint, the Python frontend emits one `llm_request` span per finished request plus engine and worker startup spans. This RFC brings the same to the Rust frontend, so swapping frontends yields the same traces in Jaeger. It needs no engine or protocol change.

_Refs: roadmap #44280. Supersedes #44567._

## Proposed design

The request span is a frontend concern. In Python the frontend emits it, not the engine, so the Rust frontend emits it too and nothing on the wire or in the engine changes. This is what #44567 got wrong. It pushed trace headers to the engine, which never emits the span.

Emit it where the data already sits: the request-finish point in the `llm` layer, where the frontend already computes the latency breakdown for Prometheus. The span reuses those numbers, so metrics and tracing cannot drift. Emitting there relaxes that crate's thin-passthrough doc comment, which is reasonable since it already emits per-request metrics from the same point. The only input that lives higher up is the caller's trace context, which the serving layer reads and threads down. Attribute names and the rule for which finishes get a span both mirror Python.

The exporter is the standard OpenTelemetry SDK with `opentelemetry-otlp`, reusing the tonic and hyper already in the workspace, so there is no second network stack. gRPC is the default, with http/protobuf as the other option, matching Python.

Engine and worker startup spans are not the frontend's to emit. The engine already produces them through its own OTel once it sees the endpoint in its environment, so the frontend only passes that variable through to the engine process.

## Plan

Seven PRs. PRs in the same phase are independent and can land in parallel.

Phase 1:

- [x] `arrival_time` fix. Stamp `arrival_time` at render/tokenize lowering to match Python. This grows the existing TTFT and e2e histograms, so it lands on its own metrics-parity merit.
- [ ] exporter bootstrap. Add the OTel crates, init the provider with the `vllm.*` resource attributes, graduate `--otlp-traces-endpoint`, and wire the gRPC exporter with a bounded shutdown flush.

Phase 2:

- [ ] request span. Extract the parent context per surface, thread it and arrival_time to the finish point, emit `llm_request`, and fill the southbound trace headers. Suppresses all aborts for now. Needs the `arrival_time` fix and exporter bootstrap.
- [ ] http/protobuf transport. Add the hyper-client exporter and protocol selection off `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL`. Needs the exporter bootstrap.
- [ ] engine and worker startup spans. Set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` for the engine children so they emit their own spans through the engine's existing Python OTel. Needs the exporter bootstrap.

Phase 3:

- [ ] abort taxonomy. Add a `client_initiated` marker so the span keeps engine-lifecycle aborts but drops client aborts, matching Python. Needs the request span.

Phase 4:

- [ ] abort metrics parity. Reuse the marker to stop counting client aborts in the finished-request metrics, matching Python. Needs the abort taxonomy.


### Feedback Period

_No response_

### CC List

cc @BugenZhao @njhill

title: [Feature]: Request observer hook for the Rust frontend
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

We run vLLM behind an API gateway and collect per-tenant usage records (prompt / cached / generated tokens) in an L7 proxy in front of it today. With the Rust frontend we would rather do this in process, as an out-of-tree module (a small crate that plugs into the frontend and writes usage records to our own store): the frontend knows the exact token counts without parsing responses, including for streams the client aborts before the final usage chunk is sent, which a proxy never sees. We don't want to patch vLLM for this, so upstream would only need a narrow, generic hook.

In the Python frontend this is possible out of tree: a stat logger plugin (`vllm.stat_logger_plugins`) receives per-request `FinishedRequestStats`, and `--middleware` can map the tenant by request id. The Rust frontend has no equivalent hook. (One gap on the Python side: requests aborted by the frontend, e.g. on client disconnect, are removed in `OutputProcessor.abort_requests` without finished stats, so they never reach stat loggers although they consumed tokens. The Rust frontend already records these aborts in Prometheus from `Drop`, so the hook below covers them.)

Today the terminal request data is computed in `RequestMetricsTracker::record_finished` and written straight to Prometheus, so nothing else can consume it. Prometheus is aggregated (no per-request or per-tenant data), and traces are sampled; the tracing plan in RFC #44757 also leaves client-initiated aborts out of the `llm_request` span, which is reasonable for tracing but means aborted streams, which still consume tokens, can't be metered from spans.

Proposal: two small, independent pieces.

**1. `vllm-llm`: a request-completion seam.** Both terminal points of `GenerateOutputStream` (`poll_next` on engine finish, `Drop` on frontend abort or stop-string match) produce one `FinishedRequest` (external / engine request id, model, LoRA, engine index, finish reason, token counts, lifecycle timestamps). The built-in Prometheus recording derives its latency breakdown from the same `FinishedRequestStats`, so metrics and other consumers cannot drift, which is the property RFC #44757 wants between metrics and the `llm_request` span. Registered observers are called synchronously, in registration order, at most once per request; panics are isolated. With no observer registered there is no extra allocation.

```rust
pub trait RequestObserver: Send + Sync + 'static {
    /// Called on the request path (possibly inside `Drop`); must not block.
    fn on_finished(&self, request: &Arc<FinishedRequest>);
    /// Called once after the engine client has shut down, e.g. to drain a queue.
    fn shutdown(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, ()> { /* no-op */ }
}

impl Llm {
    pub fn with_request_observers(self, observers: RequestObservers) -> Self;
}
```

**2. `vllm-server`: register observers the same way as the router extension (#43774).** `ServeExtensions` (router extension + request observers) and `serve_with_extensions`; `serve` and `serve_with_router_extension` keep their behavior and delegate to it. Like
#43774, this is a composition hook for custom binaries, not a stable plugin API.

**Non-goals:** no engine protocol change, no new Prometheus metrics, no queueing or async adapter upstream (I/O-bound observers hand requests to their own task; the OTel SDK already batches spans), and no per-request attribute plumbing through the request types.

### Alternatives

- OTLP spans or logs as the metering source: spans are sampled and client aborts are left out (as planned in #44757), so they are not billing-grade. With this hook, a span emitter is just another observer.
- Scraping Prometheus: aggregated, no per-request or per-tenant data.
- Patching the frontend downstream: works, but every deployment re-patches `request_metrics.rs` / `output.rs`.

### Additional context

- Prototype: an out-of-tree crate on top of the two changes writes per-tenant usage records to a Redis Stream (the tenant is attached by a router-extension middleware keyed by request id, so no upstream change is needed for that). Verified with `vllm-mock-engine`: normal finish, client abort, Redis outage, and flush on SIGTERM.
- Both changes are small and additive: one new module plus wiring at the two terminal points in `vllm-llm`, and one new module plus entry-point wiring in `vllm-server`. Existing APIs keep their behavior; I have a working branch and would split it into two PRs.
- Related: RFC #44757 (this could serve as the base for the Phase 2 `llm_request` span; happy to coordinate with @tahsintunan), #47810, #43641 / #43774.
- #54144 and #57582 touch the same files; I would rebase onto them rather than race them.
- Disclosure: the prototype was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). If this direction sounds reasonable, I'll open the PRs myself, having reviewed every change, and follow up on review feedback.

I've tried this on vllm, vllm nightly and

```
uv pip install "git+https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git@1ab2801ddebe31b75dd6022c69113b610bbdc950" --torch-backend=auto
```

Llama.cpp and ik_llama.cpp do not suffer from this fate.
